articles.title: Anvisa restringe uso compassivo da polilaminina após óbitos e alta de pedidos
articles.summary:
A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) endureceu as regras para o acesso compassivo à polilaminina — modalidade que permite o acesso a produtos ainda em fase de investigação fora de ensaios clínicos —, substância experimental investigada para o tratamento de lesões medulares. A medida foi adotada após o registro de óbitos entre pacientes que receberam o produto fora dos critérios de pesquisa e diante de uma escalada inédita de pedidos de liberação. As notificações de complicações começaram logo nos primeiros meses do ano. Entre janeiro e março de 2026, a Anvisa recebeu o comunicado de cinco óbitos quando apenas 19 pacientes haviam recebido a polilaminina por uso compassivo.
A polilaminina é obtida a partir da laminina, proteína que ajuda a sustentar as células, e é estudada para estimular a regeneração de conexões nervosas em pessoas paraplégicas ou tetraplégicas, por meio de um procedimento complexo aplicado diretamente na medula espinhal.
Óbitos registrados
O laboratório Cristália informou ter registrado oito mortes entre os pacientes tratados, todas notificadas à agência e analisadas por sua equipe de farmacovigilância. A empresa assegura que não há relação causal entre os óbitos e a polilaminina, atribuindo-os a complicações inerentes a quadros de lesão medular grave (como sepse, pneumonia, embolia pulmonar e paradas cardíacas). articles.title: Après PHP, une autre brique essentielle du web doit être mise à jour d'urgence
articles.summary:
C’est la panique sur Internet depuis ce 21 octobre 2026. La raison : deux failles critiques ont été repérées dans le langage informatique PHP, utilisé par des centaines de millions de sites web à travers le monde. La situation se révèle être un vrai casse-tête pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné qu’il est souvent difficile de repérer le langage PHP, omniprésent, mais souvent invisible. En attendant les correctifs, certains sites ont tout simplement décidé de suspendre leur accès, craignant des cyberattaques. C’est notamment le cas d’Orange qui, après avoir connu une panne majeure, a annoncé la suspension temporaire de certains de ses sites et applications par mesure de sécurité. Et la situation ne semble pas vraiment s’arranger pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné que le projet Node.js vient de publier en urgence une série de correctifs de sécurité.
Node.js corrige 10 failles de sécurité, dont quatre critiques
Node.js est un environnement d’exécution qui permet de faire fonctionner du JavaScript en dehors d’un navigateur web, notamment sur des serveurs. Node.js est bien moins répandu que le langage PHP, mais il occupe tout de même une certaine place dans l’Internet mondial. Selon les données de W3Techs du 9 septembre 2026, Node.js est utilisé comme serveur web par 7 % des sites dont le serveur est identifié. Cette proportion atteint toutefois 22 % parmi les 1 000 sites les plus fréquentés. Les risques de perturbation du web mondial sont donc réels en cas de cyberattaque.

articles.summary:
Artemis 2: Kommandant gesteht „schreckliche“ Angst – in diesem Moment
Die Artemis-2-Mission zum Mond hat für großes Aufsehen gesorgt, von einem Aufbruch in eine neue Ära war die Rede, oft fiel das Wort „historisch“. Die Nasa übertrug die Mission per Livestream, wodurch die Öffentlichkeit die Besatzung virtuell begleiten konnte.
Doch sie hatte auch Schattenseiten – und zwar für die direkt Beteiligten. Der Kommandant der Mission, Reid Wiseman, hatte Angst, die Besatzung könnte nicht mehr zur Erde zurückkehren. Auf dem Starmus-Festival auf Teneriffa (Spanien) erzählte der 50-jährige Astronaut von seinen Ängsten – und konnte sogar einen genauen Moment benennen, als diese am größten waren: als die Crew die Rückseite des Mondes umrundete.
Artemis-2-Kommandant: „Ich hatte schreckliche Angst“
Das Kontrollzentrum in Houston hatte der Crew mitgeteilt, dass die maximale Entfernung von der Erde 219.667 Seemeilen (knapp 407.000 Kilometer) betragen würde. „Ich beobachtete die Anzeige, und als sie 219.667 erreichte, dachte ich: ‚Großartig, das ist der am weitesten von der Erde entfernte Punkt; der nächste Wert wird 219.666 sein – wir sind auf dem Rückweg.‘“ Doch daraus wurde erst einmal nichts, denn rund drei Minuten später stand auf der Anzeige 219.668. Der Wert stieg weiter an. Wisemans Gedanken dazu: „Moment mal, das ist aber seltsam.“

articles.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
articles.summary:
Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
Today, Cloudflare is launching a post-quantum geographically restricted key manager in support of our Data Localization Suite (DLS) in closed beta. This new PQ GeoKey Manager is a cornerstone of Cloudflare’s data sovereignty solutions, making sure that a customer's decryption keys are only accessible in their chosen geography. GeoKey Manager implements this by wrapping each decryption key such that it can only be decrypted by Cloudflare servers that are located in the allowed geography.
While general availability (GA) is planned for Q1 2027, today’s launch is an important milestone on our journey to support our customers’ data sovereignty goals while also migrating all Cloudflare products to post-quantum (PQ) cryptography.
Governments, financial institutions, healthcare providers, and defense organizations process highly sensitive data that can remain sensitive for years or decades after it is produced. Encryption is often required to protect this data. When classical, public-key encryption is used, adversaries do not immediately need a quantum computer today to put that data at risk: they can store the ciphertext and retain them until quantum computers can break the public key cryptography protecting it — an attack strategy known as harvest now, decrypt later.

articles.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
articles.summary:
Prince of Persia, a threat group sponsored by the Iranian government, ran one of its command-and-control (C&C) servers from the United States this year, after a months-long lull in its operations, according to Semperis.
The APT actor, also tracked as Infy, has been operating for close to 20 years. Its targets are mostly Iranian dissidents, along with government and private entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East.
Tomer Bar, AVP of security research at Semperis, tracked the group in his previous role at SafeBreach. He says that within a week of SafeBreach’s February 2026 report, the hackers took a C&C server offline and later relocated the rest of their servers.
Prince of Persia then halted operations for three months, a longer silence than any other in its nearly two-decade history. The pause overlapped with the war between Iran and the US and Israel, which broke out on February 28.
Semperis told SecurityWeek that this is the longest downtime it has confirmed, as its researchers were monitoring the group’s infrastructure the entire time. Earlier quiet periods reflected gaps in researchers’ visibility into the group’s operations rather than confirmed inactivity.
Prince of Persia’s operations restarted on May 27 with the deployment of a new C&C server, and data theft resumed. Within seven days, Tonnerre, one of the group’s malware families, had siphoned over 1,800 files from a single victim.

Neues Leben für alte iPods: Diese Software-Lösungen sind besser als die von Apple
Spätestens mit der Vorstellung des Widescreen-iPods mit Touch-Eingabe, des „revolutionären“ Mobiltelefons und des Internet-Communicators, waren die Zeiten des iPods vorbei. Schließlich handelt es sich dabei um das erste iPhone, das – wie Steve Jobs mehrfach wiederholte – einen iPod bereits eingebaut hatte. Heutzutage sorgt ironischerweise genau dieses Gerät dafür, dass Nutzer:innen wieder verstärkt zum iPod greifen – auch noch pünktlich zum 25-jährigen Jubiläum. Schließlich handelt es sich dabei um ein sogenanntes „Single Purpose Device“, ein Gadget, das nur einen Zweck erfüllt: ohne ständige Unterbrechung durch Nachrichten und Social Media Musik hören zu können.
Doch wie kommt heutzutage die Musik auf den iPod? Früher hat man dafür iTunes genutzt. Seit macOS Catalina handelt es sich dabei aber nur noch um einen Shop für Musik. Wir zeigen, wie du deinen alten iPod mit Bordmitteln wieder mit Musik bespielst – und welche Apps den Job noch besser erledigen.

Microsoft’s new voice AI can start working out what you want before you finish speaking
“I think you said, ‘representative.’” It’s the fastest way to bypass automated speech recognition chatbots that fail to route human callers to the service they need. Achieving a human handoff to a living, breathing representative still feels like a badge of honor.
Microsoft wants to change that dynamic.
Naomi Moneypenny, senior director of product development at Microsoft Foundry Models division, blogged on October 1 to introduce three new Microsoft AI (MAI) models in Microsoft Foundry, Redmond’s app and agent model catalog and platform.
“A voice agent has to do more than hear a request and produce a reply. It has to keep the interaction moving while it listens, reasons, uses tools, and speaks. A delay at either end can turn a conversation into a series of awkward pauses,” writes Moneypenny.

articles.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
articles.summary:
Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
A video player seeking to the middle of a movie asks for a few megabytes. Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left. Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale.
So we rebuilt how our cache handles them. For R2, Cloudflare's object storage, p99 time to first byte dropped by about half, and a follow-up improvement cut tiered cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.
Today, we're making that new implementation available as Origin Range Requests, a self-service feature on all plans. There's no range size to tune and no need to contact support. Turn it on with a Cache Rule, and Cloudflare handles the rest.
A request for part of a file
An HTTP range request asks for part of a resource instead of the whole resource. The client sends a normal GET with a Range header:
GET /movie.mp4 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Range: bytes=1048576-2097151
If the server supports the request, it returns 206 Partial Content and identifies the returned bytes with Content-Range:
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range: bytes 1048576-2097151/524288000
Content-Length: 1048576

articles.title: La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
articles.summary:
La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
Des chercheurs de l'Université de Nankai ont dévoilé une batterie au lithium qui fonctionne encore par −70 °C et stocke deux fois plus d'énergie que les modèles actuels. Le secret : un électrolyte qui rompt avec un siècle de chimie. La découverte est spectaculaire, mais encore loin de nos voitures.
Tout conducteur de voiture électrique connaît la mauvaise surprise de l'hiver. Un matin de gel, l'autonomie affichée fond de 20, parfois 40 %, et la recharge s'éternise. Ce n'est pas un défaut de fabrication, mais une limite physique que l'on croyait presque indépassable : le froid paralyse la chimie interne des batteries. C'est précisément ce verrou, vieux comme la batterie elle-même, qu'une équipe chinoise affirme avoir fait sauter.
Pourquoi le froid tue les batteries
Pour comprendre l'exploit, il faut regarder ce qui se passe àl'intérieur d'une batterie quand le thermomètre chute. Le cœur du système, c'est l'électrolyte, ce liquide dans lequel voyagent les ions lithium d'un bout à l'autre de la cellule à chaque charge et décharge. Dans toutes les batteries actuelles, ce liquide repose sur des solvants à base d'oxygène, un choix hérité des débuts de la chimie des piles.

articles.title: Lab testing giant Quest Diagnostics confirms patients' personal and health data was compromised during breach | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Medical lab testing giant Quest Diagnostics has confirmed a cyberattack and data breach affecting an as-yet unspecified amount of sensitive patient information stored in its systems, according to a legally required disclosure with U.S. regulators.
Quest said in an 8-K filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it learned of a cyberattack on Wednesday targeting one of its lab testing systems, Quanum, which allows doctors’ offices, hospitals, and healthcare practices to request lab tests for patients while also handling billing. The platform stores a large amount of patient health and medical records, as well as associated diagnostic and billing data.
The company said the unauthorized access included the accessing of “certain patient records.” Quest said it notified law enforcement and is investigating.
The cyberattack on Quest is the latest major cyber incident to affect the healthcare industry this year. A series of cyberattacks and data breaches have sparked weeks of disruption and allowed the theft of millions of patient electronic health records and other medical information. Health tech companies have become a major target for financially motivated cybercriminals, who aim to steal as much sensitive data as possible and threaten to publish it if they aren’t paid a ransom.

Die Bundesregierung plant die “digitale Brieftasche” für alle. Für die “d-you” genannte Wallet hat sie Mitte Oktober die gesetzlichen Grundlagen geschaffen, der Bundesrat muss noch zustimmen.
Starten soll die App bereits zum 2.Januar 2027. Damit setzt Deutschland Vorgaben aus der EU um. D-you ist also die deutsche Version der European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI-Wallet), entwickelt wird sie von SPRIND und Common Codes im Auftrag des vom Bundesministerium für Digitales und Staatsmodernisierung (BMDS).
Die Nutzung ist freiwillig. Wer kein Smartphone hat oder das digitale Angebot einfach nicht nutzen will, kann also weiter auf die physischen Ausweisdokumente zurückgreifen. Nutzen lässt sich d-you ab 16 Jahren und nur auf einem Smartphone mit NFC und Android oder iOS, alternative Betriebssysteme werden nicht unterstützt. Außerdem braucht die Ausweisfunktion eine Internetverbindung. Geht das Handy verloren, muss die Wallet ohne Backup komplett neu eingerichtet werden.
Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Ab Ende 2027 sind dann auch Banken, Energieversorger, Telekommunikationsanbieter und sehr große Online-Plattformen verpflichtet, die Wallet zu nutzen. Normale Online-Shops entscheiden dagegen selbst, ob sie d-you integrieren.

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
articles.summary:
Remember Popcorn Time, the app that served as an easy-to-use front end for streaming torrents of movies and TV shows? Development of the MPAA’s least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years, but the “Netflix of Piracy” software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called “Time4Popcorn” still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.
Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
What old and vulnerable software might be running on your PC right now?
Eye Security’s Niels Teusink says the updater could have been used to install and run basically any kind of software with full privileges, easily enabling someone to create a botnet just by taking over one of the domains, using a man-in-the-middle attack to target specific devices, or perform surveillance by identifying the machines running the software.
Their solution was to register one of the domains and use it to send their own update that instructed the updater to disable itself. Despite ethical concerns about the fix, the researchers say their only alternative “was to do nothing,” pointing out, “The update process wasn’t doing anything functional anyway, it was only creating risk for users.”

Para votar no segundo turno, em 25 de outubro, o eleitor precisa estar com a situação regular no Cadastro Eleitoral. A falta das digitais registradas, por si só, não impede a votação.

articles.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Fresh Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
LiteLLM was compromised in a fresh supply chain attack, and malicious packages were served to its users on both PyPI and Docker.
The incident occurred on October 21 and involved version 1.107.0 of the popular open source proxy for routing requests across LLM providers.
The malicious packages were online for roughly three hours and are estimated to have been downloaded over 49,000 times. The packages were removed from PyPI, and Docker Hub tags and image variants were either removed or repointed to clean artifacts.
[Read: Trivy, Not LiteLLM Behind the 2,500 Org Compromise ]
Per LiteLLM’s investigation, the attackers obtained the GitHub CLI OAuth tokens for “an unexpected, innocuously named user account in our internal LiteLLM deployment, which was exposed to the public internet”.
The tokens were likely leaked by Claude Code, which, in specific circumstances, would embed them into a response body, which may be logged to LiteLLM logs. The attackers likely retrieved the tokens from the logs.
However, it is still unclear how the attackers accessed the internal deployment or moved laterally, as they had access to three sets of developer GitHub CLI credentials, LiteLLM says.
The attackers used the compromised credentials to disable branch protections, merge a change that pointed the releaser to a different source repository, and run a compromised GitHub workflow that pointed to a lookalike repository, then signed and published the poisoned artifacts.

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. But what if there was a way to start lowering those emissions even before a facility is turned on? According to two cleantech advocates, greening the data centre boom starts with the buildings, and the huge amounts of concrete used to create them.
Concrete is responsible for roughly eight percent of the world’s carbon emissions, according to a study by Chatham House. Those emissions come primarily from the process of refining cement, the binding agent used in concrete. Traditional cement is created through a combustion process that both directly releases CO2 into the atmosphere and relies heavily on fossil fuels throughout manufacturing.
“If we’re looking at the concrete and steel that’s going to go into this project, we’re looking at somewhere between 218,000 and 263,000 tonnes of CO2.”
Gil Yaron, Light House
Data centres use a lot of concrete. According to Gil Yaron, the managing director of circular innovation at Light House, a Vancouver-based non-profit supporting regenerative building practices, Meta’s Sturgeon County data centre is predicted to require as much as 1.5 million cubic metres of concrete. That’s roughly the equivalent of 37 CN Towers.
Far from just an enormous physical footprint, that translates into a lot of emissions, according to Yaron.

New research by Samsung shows calls and texts are no longer the primary use of smartphones for almost a quarter of Australians aged 18 to 24.
For 22 per cent of young Australians between 18 and 24, calls and texts – the first features enabled when mobile phones became a popular consumer product – is now not the top priority.
For everyone else, calls and texts as the main use of their device have fallen from 67 per cent in 2019 to 53 per cent in 2026.
This is a significant shift in how Australians use mobile phone technology.
The study shows smartphones are increasingly becoming more work-centric but also designed for entertainment, creativity, and everyday life.
As a result Australians are demanding more from their mobile devices than ever before.
The change in behaviour in the past seven years has coincided with the period when Samsung released its first foldable phone.
In fact, foldable phones have emerged as the new all-in-one solution for productivity, creativity, and entertainment.
Apple has also just entered the foldable market with the release of the iPhone Duo.
It will certainly bring a lot more attention to the category and attract more customers to adopt the new form factor.
Social media recorded the biggest increase as a primary smartphone usage, rising from 17 per cent in 2019 to 24 per cent in 2026.
Meanwhile smartphone use for work purposes increased by more than 50 per cent in the same period.

articles.title: La compañía de gafas neerlandesa es el primer minorista en retirar las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban de Meta de más de 400 tiendas debido a “preguntas que se han planteado” sobre la tecnología
articles.summary:

Quieren esperar hasta que se aclare cómo se pueden utilizar estos dispositivos que pueden captar a las personas que les rodean sin que estas se den cuenta, ha declarado un portavoz de la empresa, citando “las preguntas que se plantean sobre las condiciones en las que esta tecnología puede utilizarse”. articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary:
AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

articles.title: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Exposed ‘Certain Patient Records’
articles.summary:
Medical laboratory operator Quest Diagnostics said it learned of a cyber breach of one of its systems this week, likely compromising some records for patients.
In a Thursday regulatory filing, Quest Diagnostics reported “unauthorized access” to its Quanum Lab Services Manager, a platform where certain clients can place test orders and receive or look up their results. The company said it discovered the hack on Wednesday and notified federal law enforcement.
How many patients and which particular records have been affected is still unknown. Quest Diagnostics said it believes “certain patient records” were accessed in the breach, but that the full scope remains under investigation.
The New Jersey-based company said it’s also working with external cybersecurity experts to assist in its response.
Quest Diagnostics has seen hacks impacting patient records before. In 2016, for example, the company said data including lab results and contact information of about 34,000 people was exposed in another online breach. And in 2019, other personal information belonging to about 11.9 million Quest patients was affected after a separate hack at American Medical Collection Agency, a billing collections service provider.
Cyberattacks are on the rise across industries. Beyond healthcare, other breaches have recently disrupted anything from supermarket chains to core education applications.

A few engineers asked IT for Linux. Then it spread to 200 machines.
Linux is already part of the AI developer’s desktop toolkit. Nvidia’s DGX Spark, which became available to order on October 15, 2025, runs the Ubuntu-based DGX OS. OpenAI’s Codex CLI already supports Linux, another example of AI tools meeting developers where they work.
There’s just one problem. Developers can fall in love with Linux at home. Getting enterprise IT to let them use it at work is another matter.
Angelo Huang, founder and CEO of Swif.ai, a platform that manages and secures employee devices, wants to change that. Huang tells The New Stack that giving developers Linux machines starts with giving IT teams the controls to manage and secure them.
Huang says that starting this past week, Swif began expanding its Linux device management and compliance capabilities, adding Omarchy and Linux Mint support to its roster. Swif is also optimizing the onboarding process across supported Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android environments. They claim that it now takes under 10 minutes to set up device compliance standards such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.
“Linux already runs much of the infrastructure behind AI,” Huang says. “Increasingly, developers want it on their desks too. The problem isn’t that Linux can’t be secure. It’s that enterprise IT needs to be able to manage it, enforce controls, and prove those controls are working for their compliance requirements. That’s the gap we’re closing.”

articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Deploying a trained neural network involves more than translating each operator into a GPU kernel. It is a compilation problem with many legitimate answers. For example, when NVIDIA TensorRT builds an engine, it makes interdependent decisions about graph-IR transformations, fusion, implementation selection, memory placement, and quantization. This process is called scheduling. Different scheduling choices can preserve model semantics yet produce very different inference performance, making scheduling central to deep learning compiler optimization.
No single scheduling strategy is best for every model and deployment environment. A transformation that accelerates one network may slow another. A kernel that is faster in isolation may interact poorly with fusion, tensor layouts, or memory traffic elsewhere in the graph. Aggressive scheduling may improve performance while violating an application’s accuracy requirement. These coupled, model-dependent effects often appear only after the complete engine is built and measured, making the right strategy increasingly difficult to predict.
This post is Part 1 of a two-part series that is intended to develop a clearer way of reasoning about performance optimization. It explores questions such as: What makes one compiled engine better than another? Why can individually promising decisions fail end to end? How should accuracy constrain performance optimization? It introduces the Global Performance Tuner, a feature for automatic performance…

articles.title: Amazon já vendeu toda sua capacidade de nuvem até 2027
articles.summary:
A Amazon Web Services (AWS), divisão de computação em nuvem da gigante de tecnologia norte-americana, está enfrentando dificuldades para acompanhar a forte demanda impulsionada pelo avanço da inteligência artificial. Segundo o CEO da Amazon, Andy Jassy, a capacidade de processamento em nuvem da empresa já está praticamente esgotada até 2027, com compromissos significativos estendendo-se até 2028.
A declaração foi dada durante participação do executivo em um videocast promovido por Ben Horowitz e Erik Torenberg, da firma de investimentos Andreessen Horowitz. Na entrevista, Jassy destacou o apetite insaciável por infraestrutura vinda tanto de laboratórios dedicados ao desenvolvimento de IA quanto de grandes corporações.
Investimentos Bilionários
De acordo com a Reuters, para tentar suprir a demanda global, a Amazon já havia anunciado a previsão de investir cerca de US$ 220 bilhões em despesas de capital (CapEx) para 2026. No entanto, diante do cenário atual, o executivo ponderou que a empresa poderia expandir ainda mais esse montante.
“Poderíamos investir muito mais e não seria um mau uso de capital”, afirmou Jassy, ressaltando que os volumes de grande porte de capacidade em nuvem para 2026 já foram totalmente vendidos.
“2027 está em grande parte esgotado. Sempre reservamos uma certa quantia para atendimentos sob demanda e para serviços como o Bedrock e o EC2, mas os grandes blocos de capacidade já estão praticamente comprometidos. Até mesmo uma boa fatia de 2028 já foi vendida…

articles.title: Una novela premiada con 20.000 euros resultó estar escrita en un 99% por inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
La novela corta “Donde el agua trabaja”, del escritor peruano David Silva Rojas, fue escrita en un 99% por inteligencia artificial, según el detector Pangram. La obra había ganado en julio el primer Premio Internacional de Novela Breve Almadía Ventosa-Arrufat, dotado con 20.000 euros, según informó este viernes el diario español El País.
El hallazgo llevó a la editorial mexicana Almadía a suspender la presentación del libro prevista para este viernes en Madrid, así como el resto de la gira por Barcelona, Sevilla y Cádiz. El País calificó el caso como el primero de este calibre detectado en la literatura en español.
El premio fue convocado en noviembre de 2025 por Almadía junto a la fundación española Ventosa-Arrufat. Las bases eran explícitas: la participación implicaba declarar que la obra no había sido escrita, ni parcial ni totalmente, con herramientas de inteligencia artificial, bajo pena de descalificación en cualquier fase del proceso.
Entre 2.204 manuscritos enviados desde 22 países, el jurado eligió por unanimidad la novela de Silva Rojas, abogado e investigador de 45 años nacido en Ica. Lo integraron la escritora mexicana Cristina Rivera Garza, la argentina Selva Almada y la ecuatoriana Mónica Ojeda, quienes destacaron “el uso de los silencios” y un lenguaje de oraciones breves que evitaba “la tentación del panfleto”.

articles.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
articles.summary:
Japanese gaming company Capcom has disclosed a data breach impacting 11 million email addresses and the personal information of a small number of individuals.
The incident, the gaming giant says, was discovered on October 19 and involved unauthorized access to CAPCOM ID, its shared service used for accessing online services and for playing online games.
During the intrusion, the hackers stole the email addresses of 11,774,247 people, along with account data such as creation date, last login date, number of logins, and the last login’s IP address.
For 43 of the affected customers, the hackers also compromised dates of birth, gender information, country/region details, and nicknames.
Additionally, Capcom determined that the attackers changed the CAPCOM ID account passwords for 196 of the affected users. The company says that no user passwords were compromised and that it has already reset the passwords for the affected accounts.
Capcom says it implemented incident response measures and all services using CAPCOM ID remain available.
“In addition, we have started to contact the target customers sequentially, and we have established a dedicated contact point for customers regarding this matter,” an automated translation of Capcom’s incident notice reads.
The gaming company says it has reported the data breach to the relevant authorities and continues to investigate it.
It also warns the affected users to be wary of unsolicited email messages impersonating the company or related en…

articles.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
articles.summary:
NgRx, the reactive state management framework for Angular, has released version 22, shipping utilities for customising Angular's resource API, dynamic deep signals for union types, a new SignalStore typing helper and ESLint v10 compatibility.
The main new addition is resource extensions, delivered through a new experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point. Angular's resource and httpResource APIs reset value() to undefined while reloading and throw when read in an error state. Resource extensions wrap an existing resource and patch only those behaviours, while preserving the original resource type.
Four built-in extensions are included, alongside a provideResourceExtensions function that registers defaults at application, route or component level. In the original RFC, Marko Stanimirović explained that changing the error behaviour is also a prerequisite for deeper SignalStore integration, as "once a resource enters the error state, any subsequent patchState call will throw because it reads value() internally".
The proposal was well received, with Manfred Steyer replying "Love it!" and suggesting an activation signal, while another commenter asked for parity with SolidJS's createResource, such as access to the current value inside the loader.

articles.title: Der Deal steht, der Security-Fragebogen nicht: So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber
articles.summary:
Security-Fragebogen bremst den Deal? So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber für Enterprise-Vertrieb
Und der Fragebogen ist erst der Anfang: Der nächste Kunde verlangt ISO 27001, ein Automotive-Kunde TISAX, ein US-Kunde SOC 2. Je größer die Kunden werden, desto mehr entscheiden schnelle und belastbare Compliance-Nachweise über den Vertriebserfolg.
Was Enterprise-Kunden wirklich prüfen
Security-Fragebögen sehen auf den ersten Blick nach vielen unterschiedlichen Anforderungen aus, drehen sich inhaltlich jedoch meist um dieselben Fragen:
- Wer darf auf welche Systeme zugreifen (Berechtigungskonzept)?
- Welche Dienstleister verarbeiten Daten (Vendor Management)?
- Wie werden Sicherheitsvorfälle behandelt und welche Löschfristen gelten?
- Welche technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen (TOMs) sind konkret umgesetzt?
Bei kleineren Deals reicht oft eine Selbstauskunft. Bei Enterprise-Kunden, regulatorischen Vorgaben (wie NIS2, DORA, dem Cyber Resilience Act oder dem EU AI Act) und branchenspezifischen Standards kommen formale Nachweise wie ISO 27001, SOC 2 oder TISAX hinzu.
Der Kunde fragt dabei nach der Kontrolle und dem Nachweis, nicht nach dem spezifischen Framework dahinter. Viele Unternehmen haben deshalb kein neues Compliance-Problem, sondern ein Wiederverwendungsproblem: Wer jedes Framework als separates Projekt behandelt, beschreibt Controls neu, sucht Nachweise erneut zusammen und dokumentiert Verantwortlichkeiten mehrfach.

La compañía japonesa confirmó que dejará de fabricar el UBP-X700/K, su último reproductor Blu-ray Ultra HD que todavía se vendía en Japón. Con ello, Sony saldrá del mercado de reproductores dedicados, una jugada que forma parte de una estrategia para alejarse del formato físico.
Según recoge FlatpanelsHD, el UBP-X700/K dejó de distribuirse el 22 de octubre de 2026 y desaparecerá una vez que se agoten todas las unidades. Este modelo llegó como una actualización del UBP-X700 y era compatible con discos Ultra HD Blu-ray, HDR10, Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos y DTS:X. Sony no ha revelado si habrá un sucesor, pero todo indica que no ocurrirá, puesto que la compañía ha dejado de invertir en este tipo de reproductores debido al auge del formato digital.
Hace más de un año que la japonesa anunció que dejaría de fabricar discos Blu-ray grabables y que no tenía planes de un nuevo formato. Aunque Sony aclaró que la medida solo se aplicaría a los discos vírgenes y no a las películas o videojuegos, la realidad es que la empresa ya tenía planes de alejarse de este negocio. En junio de este año, PlayStation dio la estocada final al formato físico al anunciar que ya no lanzarían juegos en disco a partir de 2028, generando rechazo por una buena parte de la comunidad de jugadores.

articles.title: OPINION: Robotics are essential for Europe’s energy transition | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Europe’s energy transition story is usually told through assets: more renewable generation, smarter grids, electric vehicles and battery storage. Yet while much of the debate focuses on financing and building infrastructure, a different challenge is emerging beneath the surface: operating and maintaining a rapidly expanding asset base over the next several decades.
But the high-margin subsidised programmes that kick-started the industry are being phased out, and operators are facing a new reality of low-margin operations at scale. Combined with the demographic squeeze on the European workforce, the industry looks ripe for automation. Maybe even for robots.
The problem is well-known and systemic. Transmission networks are aging – some 40% of Europe’s distribution grids are over 40 years old – and cross-border capacity is set to double. Offshore wind is moving further from shore and into deeper water. Solar is multiplying faster than construction and maintenance teams can keep up with.
The jobs required to operate all of this are highly skilled or physically demanding and impossible to scale quickly: rope-access technicians, electrical engineers, subsea specialists, offshore crews. You cannot train a generation of them in a hiring cycle, and Europe’s demographics make the recruitment harder every year.

La herramienta, llamada “Pruébalo” o “Try On” en inglés, busca resolver una de las mayores desventajas de comprar ropa por internet: la imposibilidad de probársela antes de recibirla en casa.

La función está desarrollada por Google y funciona con un modelo de generación de imágenes especializado en moda. A diferencia de un montaje simple, la herramienta interpreta la postura, las proporciones corporales y la caída de la tela para generar una representación más realista del resultado final.
“La herramienta conserva estas sutilezas cuando se aplican las prendas a poses en tus fotos, por lo que el resultado te permite ver cómo luciría en ti, en lugar de ver sólo una imagen fija o en un modelo”, detalló Google.
La función permite probar tops, pantalones, vestidos y zapatos, y da acceso a miles de millones de artículos disponibles en el inventario de Shopping de la compañía.

articles.title: Anthropic Adds Opt-In Security Scanning for Critical Open-Source Projects

AI company Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service to find vulnerabilities in open-source projects. Enrolled maintainers receive periodic security reports generated by the company's strongest models, including Claude Mythos. The reports are sent without human review, and project maintainers can choose to validate their findings and decide which proposed fixes to accept.
In its 8th October announcement, Anthropic's Frontier Red Team explains that human validation has become a constraint. Over six months, its models identified more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities, but researchers manually reviewed and triaged approximately 6,000. Maintainers who wanted earlier access had already received nearly 5,000 unverified reports, together with proposed patches, after asking for them.
Each scanner report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the suspected vulnerability. Where possible, it identifies the change that introduced the bug through bisection and supplies a candidate patch. This extends work conducted through Project Glasswing, which InfoQ covered in April when Anthropic restricted Mythos Preview access to participating organisations.

“VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-prem has a security issue where this issue may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host,” Arista notes in its advisory.
Successful exploitation could impact the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of both VCO and the data it manages.

All VCO releases before versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12 are affected. Arista has already patched the hosted VCO deployments, but urges users to update their on-premises installations as soon as possible.
“This issue was detected by Arista and is known to be actively exploited,” the company says.

articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
The Global Performance Tuner is a feature for automatic performance tuning released in NVIDIA TensorRT 11.1. It provides automatic, accuracy-aware and end-to-end performance tuning within TensorRT by customizing different optimizations for different models. For more details, see Part 1 of this series, which introduces the challenges associated with scheduling (a critical stage in deep learning compiler optimization), the motivation for developing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT, and the mathematical theories established to formalize the problem.
This post, Part 2, uses the notation from Part 1 to describe the algorithm and architectural design of the Global Performance Tuner feature. It also provides best practices for using it.
Designing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT
The central design idea of the Global Performance Tuner is to represent alternative scheduling strategies as explicit and searchable build routes. A compiler knob (also called a compiler flag or compiler option) is a configuration setting that changes some aspect of the compilation pipeline, such as a heuristic, fusion decision, or code generation path.
Each tunable knob exposes a finite set of allowed values and has a default value. A build route is a concrete combination of knob values. When no build route is specified, TensorRT uses the default build route, in which every knob retains its default value.

articles.title: Confiner l'IA devient un casse-tête : après sa pause de 11 jours, OpenAI explique pourquoi couper Internet ne suffit pas
articles.summary:
OpenAI est revenu sur la sécurité de ses modèles dans une communication publiée le 23 octobre. Les cas de « désalignement », ces comportements qui s’écartent de ce que l’on attend des IA, se sont accumulés ces derniers mois avec pas moins de 20 incidents constatés sur l’année 2026.
Chez OpenAI, des agents sont notamment parvenus à pirater Hugging Face pendant une évaluation interne. D’autres ont appris à dissimuler leurs erreurs.
En septembre, un nouvel accès non autorisé à Internet avait conduit l’entreprise à suspendre certains travaux sur ses modèles les plus avancés. OpenAI précise désormais que cette pause a duré onze jours, jusqu’au 1er octobre, pour renforcer ses protections et les mettre à l’épreuve.
Pourquoi faut-il confiner une IA pendant son entraînement ?
Trouver une information, écrire du code, résoudre un problème : pour entraîner une IA, OpenAI (et d’autres) force son modèle à trouver une solution. Le modèle essaie, échoue, recommence, et les essais réussis servent ensuite à renforcer les comportements qui l’ont mené au but. Mais comment s’assurer qu’il ne prend pas un raccourci interdit pour y arriver ?
D’où l’idée de l’enfermer dans un environnement contrôlé, souvent appelé « bac à sable ». L’IA y dispose d’outils pour travailler, mais ses accès sont limités. Un peu comme un terrain d’exercice : elle doit pouvoir s’entraîner sans intervenir sur les systèmes extérieurs.

The eight maximum-severity security flaws patched today affect multiple AOS-8 and AOS-10 software versions, and they can be exploited by remote threat actors without privileges through low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction.
HPE warned customers to patch these security issues as soon as possible and provided mitigation measures, including restricting access to AOS management interfaces.

articles.title: Cómo saber qué aplicaciones tienen acceso al micrófono de tu celular y bloquearlas
articles.summary:
Los teléfonos inteligentes permiten realizar videollamadas, grabar audios y utilizar asistentes virtuales gracias a sensores y herramientas que también pueden representar riesgos para la privacidad si se administran incorrectamente.
Por eso, revisar qué aplicaciones tienen permiso para acceder al micrófono es una medida importante para proteger la información personal y evitar usos innecesarios de esta función.
Tanto Android como iOS ofrecen opciones para consultar los permisos concedidos, restringir el acceso al micrófono y detectar cuándo una aplicación lo está utilizando. Aunque tener este permiso no significa que una aplicación esté grabando conversaciones en secreto, sí conviene comprobar qué programas lo necesitan realmente y cuáles podrían funcionar sin él.
La revisión puede realizarse desde la configuración del teléfono, sin instalar aplicaciones adicionales. También es recomendable prestar atención a los indicadores de privacidad que aparecen en la pantalla cuando el micrófono está activo.
Cómo revisar los permisos del micrófono en Android
En los celulares Android, la ruta puede variar ligeramente según el fabricante y la versión del sistema operativo, pero generalmente es posible encontrar los permisos desde los ajustes de privacidad.

Starting in early September 2026, the threat actor was seen abusing Artex to automate its attacks, and previous reporting by CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Recorded Future linked this AI-powered activity to attacks targeting South Korean financial institutions.
Now, Microsoft says Storm-0940 used Artex to automate intrusions into ConnectWise customers’ environments in mid-October. In response, ConnectWise suspended several services, including Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management.
At the time, Huntress observed the attackers using compromised ConnectWise application credentials to access hundreds of Microsoft 365 tenants, including over 300 Entra tenants.
According to Microsoft, the threat actor relied on Artex to accelerate reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse. It hit over 300 accounts across eight organizations at a pace of more than 2,900 attempts per minute.

The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. The American search and AI giant has also been told to cease work where it has cleared roughly 500 acres of forest, 55 miles southeast of the village of Otanmäki. Now The Guardian reports that wolves, who used to live in the forests, are roaming into villages neighboring these man-made muddy wastelands.
Local anger continues to simmer over the damage done to Finnish forests, as Google seems to have ridden roughshod over regulations in the hurry to build new AI data centers in Finland. However, the report suggests that it isn’t just environmentalists who have a beef with Google. Some families say wolves and other wild animals have entered the countryside villages. “We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” explained Anni Ranta, 53, whose family has lived in Otanmäki for generations. Ranta also fears the U.S.-owned data centers will make Finland an even juicier target for Russian aggression.

Not that I believe for a second that Apple will actually make a 2-in-1 convertible.

articles.title: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Cloud providers in multi-cloud systems charge for data leaving their network, not entering it. The egress costs accumulate silently and are rarely caught before deployment.
- Architecture determines egress cost more than per-unit transfer rates. Where services are placed and how often they communicate matters far more than what you negotiate on billing rates.
- FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) provides a unified billing format across cloud providers, reducing normalization effort, but service-level attribution still requires provider-specific fields, ownership metadata, and network telemetry.
- Replacing continuous cross-cloud data transfer with scheduled synchronization reduces costs significantly without degrading service performance.
- Architecture had a larger impact on cost than provider pricing. In the controlled experiment, changing the communication pattern from synchronous cross-cloud processing to near-source processing saved over $2000 per month, while changing the provider rate saved $825 per month.
Introduction
Multi-cloud architectures give teams the flexibility to optimize for availability, vendor capabilities, and geographic reach. But this flexibility carries a hidden cost due to data movement across cloud provider boundaries. The costs accumulate through service placement decisions, communication patterns, and scaling behavior compounding over time. By the time it shows up on a bill, the architectural damage is done.

articles.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?

Headlines warn that AI could threaten humanity, and it’s easy to wave that off as science fiction. But the real danger is more ordinary and already here.
Research published by Gen Threat Labs demonstrated how quickly an AI agent’s autonomy can become a liability. In a controlled experiment, researchers manipulated an agent through content it encountered while reading email, prompting it to execute system commands, transmit data outside its environment and perform destructive file operations.
No software vulnerability was required. The agent simply treated untrusted content as instruction.
That autonomy is expanding daily. Agents are moving from answering questions to taking action doing everything from executing code, connecting to services, managing files and making decisions on a user’s behalf.
The shift from developer-focused tools like OpenClaw to widespread use of personal assistants like Muse, happened quickly. Delegating work across platforms is becoming commonplace and how people interact with AI.
The risks extend beyond manipulating agents. In October, Gen Threat Labs documented Warden Stealer, malware targeting configuration files and local data associated with AI assistants and coding tools, potentially exposing credentials, access tokens and conversation histories.

Researcher Patrick Wardle has analyzed Heartbreaker, a Rust-based macOS ransomware sample that was uploaded to VirusTotal in May 2025 and, as of his writing, was still undetected by every antivirus engine on the service. articles.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
articles.summary:
The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch.
PHP is an open-source web development language used by nearly 70% of all websites on the Internet. According to VirusTotal estimates, more than 5.1 million PHP hosts are exposed online, and roughly 3.8 million have at least one port open to attacks.
According to a Friday advisory, this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-115560) can only be exploited when targeting systems "with an unusual combination of configuration and application code."
"An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled," the PHP team explained.
"Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release."
Until a security patch is available, the PHP devs suggested setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0, adding that "If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed."

articles.title: Before you expand your GPU pool, measure the outcome
articles.summary:
Before you expand your GPU pool, measure the outcome
For teams running AI workloads on Kubernetes, a fully allocated GPU pool and a growing batch-job queue might make expanding the pool seem like the obvious next step. But a growing queue could point to timing, serving capacity, or the choice of model and hardware. Before expanding a GPU pool, teams should define what success looks like, when it must finish, and what it costs to deliver.
“An allocated GPU, a busy GPU, and a workload producing valuable results are not the same thing.”
That starts with a distinction: an allocated GPU, a busy GPU, and a workload producing valuable results are not the same thing. Understanding how they relate can help teams use existing capacity more effectively before provisioning additional capacity they genuinely need.
Start with the outcome and deadline
Look at the workloads and the underlying use cases they support. A customer service chatbot may need around-the-clock inference capacity, while results from a model evaluation job might only be needed before the next internal release sync. Classifying workloads into broad categories like “inference” and “training” does not determine urgency. Some batch inference can wait, while a training job may have a firm deadline.

articles.title: Compromised TLS Certificates - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Compromised TLS Certificates
The Indian CA eMudhra Limited has eight TLS certificates with laughably weak private keys:
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2384, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
The whole certificate regime has long been a mess:
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest…

They charge for active CPU time and memory, rather than CPU time spent waiting for downstream services. Multi-Region routing directs requests to the closest Region, while a single warm execution environment can handle multiple concurrent requests, significantly reducing cold starts. Existing Lambda functions are now called Lambda Event Functions, with no changes required. Micah Walter, senior solutions architect at AWS, summarizes the benefits and why it removes this complexity:
You can take a standard port-listening server built with Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js, or any Node.js framework, deploy it with a single command, and Lambda automatically handles scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing. No adapters, no infrastructure to manage, and no framework lock-in.
Endpoints use a Lambda-provided domain by default. To use a custom domain, edge caching, or AWS WAF, developers can use Amazon CloudFront in front, relying on Lambda Web Functions as the origin.

When Derek Lubner was managing his late parents’ foundation, Make an Immediate Difference, he routinely asked beneficiary non-profit organisations to submit wish lists for the upcoming year.
If an organisation wanted cricket bats and nets, a classroom or a soccer field, the co-founder and chairman of iZinga Assist, digital non-profit verification and support platform, would consider the request and agree to fund all or part of it. Les terres rares forment un groupe de 17 métaux. Dans la croûte terrestre, elles sont dispersées, mélangées entre elles, et très difficiles à extraire comme à séparer. Un atout économique qui peut devenir une véritable arme diplomatique.
Un levier redoutable pour la Chine
Car ces métaux offrent une puissance environ dix fois supérieure à celle des aimants classiques, pour un poids et une taille réduits. On les retrouve donc partout : dans les smartphones, les voitures électriques, les éoliennes, les avions de chasse ou encore les moteurs des machines d’usine.
Et justement, d’après Reuters, TSMC, numéro 1 mondial de la fabrication de semi-conducteurs, a sondé ses fournisseurs sur des moteurs sans terres rares pour l’automatisation de ses usines. Cet échange figure parmi les démonstrations publiées par Block ce vendredi 23 octobre pour présenter Dessa. L’entreprise de Jack Dorsey (ex-fondateur de Twitter, devenu X) affirme avoir entraîné ce modèle uniquement sur des conversations humaines, sans texte ni modèle préentraîné. Les extraits sont étonnamment vivants, au point que certains internautes peinent à croire qu’ils écoutent une IA.
Une IA qui n’attend pas son tour pour parler

Dessa reproduit les imperfections de nos conversations. Sur ces extraits, choisis par Block, elle paraît plus fluide que les échanges encore assez mécaniques de Gemini, et même que les modèles vocaux de ChatGPT lancés en juillet dernier.

articles.title: Why Kubernetes autoscalers keep fighting each other (and why the solution must be autonomous)

Why Kubernetes autoscalers keep fighting each other (and why the solution must be autonomous)
Ask an SRE a deceptively simple question: What is the right size for checkout-api, and how many replicas should it run right now?
Their Helm values specify replicas: 3, cpu: 1000m, and memory: 2Gi. But the live cluster tells a different story: HPA has scaled the app to 11 replicas on CPU load; VPA insists it is over-provisioned, recommending cpu: 350m and memory: 3.1Gi; KEDA demands 24 replicas due to an upstream Kafka lag spike; and Karpenter has provisioned two new nodes, sizing physical capacity strictly against declared requests rather than actual usage.
“Five sources yield five contradictory answers. Each controller acts logically in isolation, but none sees the complete picture.”
Five sources yield five contradictory answers. Each controller acts logically in isolation, but none sees the complete picture. This gap between isolated observations and actual workload needs represents a core architectural failure in modern Kubernetes operations.
The breakdown of the Unix philosophy in elastic systems
Kubernetes and its components were built on the Unix philosophy: build small, modular tools that do one thing well. For container orchestration, this principle seemed intuitive:
- HPA handles horizontal elasticity based on runtime resource utilization.

articles.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
articles.summary:
CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon (sBeacon), a serverless architecture for querying genomic variant data without copying large genomic datasets into a central database. The system uses Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon Athena, and Amazon DynamoDB to provide an implementation of the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) Beacon standard, supporting genomic queries across large cohorts while keeping the underlying data in its original storage.
The architecture separates genomic data from the metadata needed to search it. Variant Call Format (VCF) files remain in Amazon S3, while metadata such as disease status, age, and location is indexed separately. During onboarding, sBeacon creates indexes and Athena tables for the metadata, while ontology terms are handled through CSIRO's Ontoserver to support queries combining genomic and phenotypic information.
sBeacon data onboarding architecture (Source: AWS Blog Post)
For variant queries, API Gateway routes requests to Lambda functions that identify relevant datasets and genomic regions. The Variant Querying Module uses bcftools and its htslib library to retrieve specific portions of VCF files through HTTP byte range requests. This allows the system to read the required genomic region without transferring the complete file. Results are aggregated and returned through the Beacon API.

Con ambos protocolos descifrados, la aplicación puede descubrir el reloj, activarlo, reconectarlo y sincronizarlo desde un móvil con Android. Según detalla el repositorio del proyecto en GitHub, todo el proceso de configuración inicial se completa sin recurrir a ningún dispositivo de Apple.
El emparejamiento con Android admite dos métodos: por código PIN o mediante la cámara del teléfono. El autor reutilizó los mismos protocolos reconstruidos para extender la compatibilidad a Windows, Linux y macOS, aunque estas últimas versiones son más limitadas que la de Android.

Millicent Okumu doesn’t leave you wondering whether she believes what she is saying. She speaks with energy, with clarity about whom she is building for. Ask where the company is heading, and there is little hesitation; ask whether she will still be running it in ten years, and the answer is no.
By then, she expects Agriflex, the Kenyan agricultural business she co-founded, to be operating in at least five African countries, to be sustainably profitable, and to be led by somebody else. She might take an advisory role. For now, however, the company occupies even the hours she supposedly spends away from it. At family gatherings, unfinished tasks follow her into the room.
Her father, a civil servant and farmer, raised cattle and grew enough food to support relatives beyond his household. She was close to him, but less enthusiastic about the farm. She avoided agriculture at school and university, only to find herself back in it through a logistics job at iProcure in 2017.
Now she sells farm inputs, deploys spraying drones and listens to farmers explain why a clever piece of technology might be of little use to them. That last part has meant slowing down plans and turning away investors.
“We are in 2026,” she says. “We are no longer in 2006.”
She is impatient for progress, but increasingly particular about what counts as progress, and who benefits.

articles.title: Unerwartetes Wetterphänomen: Wie sich auf dem Mars eine 1.800 Kilometer lange Wolke formt
articles.summary:
1.800 Kilometer lang und völlig ohne Staub: Das Rätsel um Mars-Wolke ist gelöst
Die europäische Weltraumorganisation Esa hat neue Daten zur sogenannten Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud veröffentlicht. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entsteht dieses langgestreckte Gebilde durch einen bisher in planetaren Atmosphären nicht beobachteten Mechanismus. Dieser physikalische Prozess, die sogenannte homogene Keimbildung, vollzieht sich gänzlich ohne die Anwesenheit von Kondensationskernen wie Staub oder Schmutzpartikeln.
Dabei galt in der meteorologischen Forschung bislang ein fester Grundsatz: Wasserdampf benötigt zwingend Staub oder andere winzige Partikel, um zu kondensieren. Da die Atmosphäre des Mars extrem staubig ist, nahmen bisherige Klimamodelle diesen Vorgang stets als alleinigen Standardmechanismus an.
Die aktuellen Computersimulationen eines Forschungsteams um Jorge Hernández-Bernal und Franck Forget von der französischen Sorbonne Université in Paris widerlegen dies nun. Sie zeigen, dass diese etablierte Grundannahme für die lange Arsia-Mons-Wolke schlichtweg nicht gilt.

Der rund 20 Kilometer hohe Vulkan Arsia Mons wirkt auf den Marswind wie eine gigantische Rampe. Wenn die Luftströmungen auf das massive Hindernis treffen, werden sie als atmosphärische Wellen mit hoher Geschwindigkeit nach oben gedrückt. Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90% while preserving load-balancing accuracy.
Cloudflare relies on consistent hashing in its Pingora Backend Router to distribute cacheable requests across servers, but supporting weighted servers and different feature combinations required many hash rings, significantly increasing memory usage. The team identified excessive memory usage coming from its pingora-ketama consistent-hashing data structures, prompting an investigation into their design and optimization.
Cloudflare applied probability theory to consistent hashing to determine the minimum number of hash points needed to achieve the required distribution, allowing the team to significantly reduce the size of the hashing structures while maintaining the required distribution.

articles.title: ‘Clayface’ es una pasable película de terror que no aporta nada al Universo DC
articles.summary:
Clayface es una película de terror a toda regla. Y una, que hace un especial buen uso del body horror en los momentos correctos. No obstante, poco o nada tiene que ver con el Universo DC en construcción y ese es su gran problema. De hecho, esta película (basada en el clásico personaje con guion de Mike Flanagan) fácilmente podría ser solo una pequeña obra de autor del género. No en vano, su director, James Watkins, crea algunas secuencias escalofriantes y ciertamente deslumbrantes, que combinan efectos prácticos con digitales. A la vez, trabaja en una atmósfera cuidadosa y bien lograda, que profundiza en la oscura psicología de su personaje.
Pero el problema radica en que Clayface no se parece ni en tono ni en forma al resto del universo al que pertenece. Por lo que, a pesar de ser inquietante, repugnante y, a grandes rasgos, terrorífica, peca de genérica. Y lo es, porque el Tom Haggen de Tom Rhys Harries podría ser cualquier personaje atormentado de la reciente ola de terror gore. Artificial Intelligence
How Bayer Crop Science built an agentic decision engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS Unified Operations
Plant breeding decisions depend on data that spans genomics, field trials, imagery, environmental conditions, and model outputs. Bayer Crop Science runs hundreds of machine learning (ML) model configurations against this data across crops, regions, and teams, and each run needs to be repeatable and governed. To meet that requirement, Bayer built the Connected Decision Engine (CDE), a system for deploying, orchestrating, monitoring, and reusing ML workflows. CDE gives breeders, analysts, researchers, data scientists, and data engineers a consistent way to run analytics while preserving execution history and operational controls.
As adoption grew, the bottleneck moved from running workflows to understanding them. Explaining a result meant piecing together context from APIs, documentation, metadata stores, dashboards, and logs. A user who wanted to know why a workflow failed, what a model did, or where a result came from still had to know which system to inspect. To close that gap, Bayer built the Agentic Decision Engine (ADE), a multi-agent, natural language interface over CDE. A supervisor agent routes each question to a specialist agent, the specialist retrieves context from the relevant system, and the user receives an answer without navigating the operational stack. Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman of EY GDS made the case that moving agents into production is an engineering problem, not a model problem.
Ask a room of developers about agents today and you will get plenty of answers. Almost everyone has built one, and most have a demo they are proud of.
The harder question is what happens after that, when the agent has to hold up against real customers, real data, and real consequences. At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman, Global Cloud Consulting, Microsoft Practice and Alliances Leader at EY GDS, opened with a version of it. He asked how many people in the room had built an AI agent, and plenty of hands went up. Then he asked how many had built one that made it to production for a business-critical system. "I think that's where the numbers dramatically drop," he said. "Not because of anybody's fault, but that's how it is."
That gap is the whole problem, and it is not a model problem. Cloud, low code tools, and open model APIs have pushed the entry barrier close to zero. What has not changed is the difficulty of industrializing what you build. "Access to intelligence is not the bottleneck, but the ability to industrialize is going to be the bottleneck," said Arvind Purushothaman.

articles.title: Plus un matériau est petit, plus il est résistant : pourquoi les nanoparticules sont mille fois plus résistantes que le même métal à notre échelle

Comme le dit le dicton, « tout ce qui est petit est mignon ». Mais il est plus rare d’entendre dire que ce qui est plus petit est plus costaud. Et pourtant c’est ce qu’il semble se passer pour de nombreux matériaux si on diminue leurs dimensions jusqu’à quelques dizaines de nanomètres (un milliardième de mètre). Des expériences et des simulations numériques montrent en effet que la résistance mécanique peut augmenter d’un facteur mille à ces échelles. Comment cela est-il possible ?
Revenons tout d’abord aux bases. Si on compresse un matériau, il se déforme généralement avec une amplitude faible et de manière élastique, c’est-à-dire réversible. Toutefois, au-delà d’un certain niveau de contrainte mécanique exercée, la déformation devient plastique donc irréversible. Ce seuil de résistance mécanique maximal dépend bien évidemment du type de matériau. L’acier est ainsi notoirement plus résistant que du plomb, et une pierre que du polystyrène. articles.title: Building an agentic software factory? Start with the sensor.

Building an agentic software factory? Start with the sensor.
A gap has long existed between the shipping velocity of the best engineering teams and the rest of the bell curve. For most of the industry’s history, it was a multiple measured in deploys per week. Agents are turning that multiple into an exponent, and the dividing line is no longer tooling or talent. It is whether a team has rebuilt its delivery system into what the industry now calls a “software factory,” a largely autonomous system where intent goes in, agents plan, write, test, and ship the changes. People own the specifications and the gates.
Anthropic put a number on the gap this month. In May the company merged around 2,500 code changes a day, and by September it merged more than 30,000. Coding stopped being the bottleneck, they write. The bottleneck became the developer infrastructure built for human scale, and they now ask what continuous integration (CI) even means when thousands of changes merge while the tests are still running.
“Agents are turning that multiple into an exponent, and the dividing line is no longer tooling or talent. It is whether a team has rebuilt its delivery system into what the industry now calls a ‘software factory.'”

Egyptian ed-tech startup Learning Rockets is helping children from pre-K to Grade 6 learn English through a connected system of books, a learning app and progress data.
The World Bank estimates that 70 per cent of 10-year-olds in Egypt cannot read and understand a simple text, while the country is rated “low proficiency” in the 2025 EF English Proficiency Index.
“In Egyptian schools, English lives in the school book and stays there,” co-founder and CEO Mariam Soliman told Disrupt Africa. “I saw three problems up close. Practice stops at the classroom door: at home, nothing connects to the lesson a child just learned. The apps parents download are fun, but they teach their own course, not the one the child is tested on. And nobody – teacher, principal or parent – sees how a child is doing until the exam. In Upper Egypt, add weak internet and old devices, and most digital products simply don’t work.”
Founded in Assiut in Upper Egypt, Learning Rockets launched the first prototype of its Bee Degree app in 2023, with the idea for the business having started at home.
“My daughter became fluent in English because we taught it to her at home, and I kept asking myself – why can’t other children in Upper Egypt have the same chance?” Soliman said. “I had spent more than 10 years in business and finance, and I decided to build that chance myself.”

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
articles.summary:
Researchers remotely disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent client, closing a security flaw that could have allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on millions of computers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-30612, affects Windows and macOS updaters that contacted the app's abandoned domain (popcorntimeupd.xyz) over unencrypted HTTP and accepted executables without verifying digital signatures.
Anyone controlling the update domain could manipulate HTTP traffic and execute code as SYSTEM on Windows and as root on macOS.
The Popcorn Time app featured a Netflix-style interface that integrated BitTorrent downloads, allowing users to consume illegal content right directly inside the app.
The project was abandoned for legal reasons but later relaunched as a legitimate content-streaming app. However, forks such as Time4Popcorn emerged under the Popcorn Time name, quickly attracting millions of users.
Researchers at Eye Security discovered the security risk after registering the popcorntimeupd.xyz domain and observed up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections to Time4Popcorn.
Connections came from residential ISPs and corporate, government, and military networks. However, none of the users appeared to be actively using the app, suggesting it had been installed and forgotten.

articles.title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
articles.summary:
Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision.
But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions.
“This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?”
To find out, Nieder and his colleague Philipp Schmidbauer put two carrion crows through the same task the monkeys faced, recording their brain activity along the way. The crows solved the task the same way primates do, using the same mathematical logic despite having a very different brain structure. And they did it two times faster.
A brain built different
Nieder and Schmidbauer put two hand-raised crows in front of a touch-sensitive monitor showing a cloud of white dots on black, with some fraction of them drifting coherently left or right or up or down. The birds’ job was to report the overall direction by pecking one of the targets that flanked the display. Correct answers earned them a mealworm.

La subcongelación suave a -3 °C se ubicó entre la refrigeración convencional, de 4 °C, y el congelamiento profundo. En carnes y pescados, esa temperatura cristalizó solo la capa externa de las proteínas.
Según Panasonic, el método que implementaron permitió conservar ingredientes durante hasta siete días sin petrificarlos. Los alimentos quedaron listos para cortar y cocinar, sin los tiempos de espera propios de la descongelación ni los cambios bruscos de ambiente asociados a la proliferación bacteriana.
