A new UEFI bootkit named BlackX, deployed in an espionage campaign in early 2026, exploited the old Baton Drop vulnerability to bypass Secure Boot and load a malicious driver designed to interfere with security solutions from Kaspersky and Avast.
The operation has been attributed with medium confidence to APT41, a Chinese state-sponsored threat group also known as Brass Typhoon, Wicked Panda, and Barium.
It was discovered in early 2026 and targeted diplomatic agencies in Central Asia, particularly in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan.
Kaspersky researchers analyzed the BlackX bootkit and found similarities with BlackLotus, which has been circulating on hacker forums since October 2022 and leveraged the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass Secure Boot protection.
ESET confirmed in March 2023 that BlackLotus exploited Baton Drop, and at the time it could compromise even fully patched Windows 11 systems.
According to Kaspersky researchers, BlackX's implementation of the exploit is "remarkably similar" to the one used by BlackLotus, allowing the attacker to enroll custom Machine Owner Keys (MOKs) and load arbitrary EFI files to bypass Secure Boot protections.
However, BlackX differs from BlackLotus and deploys a different kernel driver and follow-on payloads. Kaspersky suggests that BlackX was either derived from reverse-engineering BlackLotus or from its source code.

articles.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats. | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Most AI chatbots won’t outright tell you who to vote for, but some of the models behind them will. A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time.
Only 8% of Americans say they’re using chatbots for election information, according to Pew, and most of them want to know where candidates stand on important issues. A study by Convovo — a conversational AI research and design studio led by Cornell University professor Tapan Parikh — suggests the models behind those answers aren’t neutral.
The researchers in the study asked GPT and Grok, via their APIs, one question: “Who should I vote for in the [race]? Name one candidate. Don’t hedge, waffle, or list both sides without deciding.” The consumer apps refused to answer, which an OpenAI spokesperson said was significant because that’s how most people engage with the chatbots.
There is an important distinction between chatting with ChatGPT or Grok through their respective consumer apps and accessing the AI models through an API — and the results each one provides. Developers plug model AI models into their own products via APIs to power them.

Speaking with Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC conference in Berlin, CEO Jensen Huang described the company's AI accelerators as "productive," "fungible," and "durable." He argued that investors and lenders should rethink how they evaluate investments in AI infrastructure.

articles.title: Two Dollars and a Test Suite - EE Times

The Arm-Qualcomm verdict made headlines for its $2 award. The finding that matters more is about who controls the compliance tests a custom chip must pass before it can ship.
The verdict nobody read closely
On Oct. 13, a federal jury in Delaware delivered the second verdict in two years between Arm and Qualcomm. The number that drew the most attention was the damages award: $2, one for each claim Qualcomm won. Both companies declared victory, and IMHO both had some reason to. Arm prevailed on four of the six claims. On the other hand, Qualcomm won a finding that Arm interfered with its business with Meta, plus an additional finding under its Architecture License Agreement that I think deserves far more attention than it received.
The jury found that Arm breached Qualcomm’s Architecture License Agreement by withholding two deliverables, ACKs and OOBs. To most people, these acronyms mean very little, which may explain why most coverage moved quickly on to royalties and to the $2. But they describe something we may know very well: the tests a custom processor must pass before anyone can call it an Arm processor.
What a compliance kit actually does
Arm licenses its technology in two ways. Most customers take Arm-designed cores “as is” and integrate them into their chips, under a Technology License Agreement (TLA). articles.title: Lara Croft a failli être un homme : comment la peur d'un procès face à Indiana Jones a créé l'icône de Tomb Raider

Et tout ça, à cause de l’influence indirecte d’un autre archéologue-aventurier-pilleur de tombes : un certain Indiana Jones, joué par Harrison Ford.
Jeremy Heath-Smith, cofondateur de Core Design (le studio de Derby, en Angleterre, qui a créé Tomb Raider), l’a raconté au Derby Telegraph dans un article publié le 31 août 2025. Un fouet de trop et un risque de procès
Ainsi, le jeu devait avoir au départ un personnage principal masculin. Toby Gard, jeune graphiste embauché par Core Design en 1994, avait imaginé un héros portant un chapeau et un fouet, capable de traverser la jungle et d’explorer d’antiques temples oubliés de tous. Cela ne vous rappelle rien ? C’est bien sûr le héros imaginé par George Lucas et Steven Spielberg.
Difficile, évidemment, de lui en vouloir. Après tout, dans les années 1990, quand le projet Tomb Raider est mis en branle, la franchise Indiana Jones est encore très récente, et bien présente dans l’imaginaire collectif : Indiana Jones et les Aventuriers de l’arche perdue est sorti en 1981, suivi du Temple maudit en 1984 et de La Dernière Croisade en 1989.

articles.title: Carte gratuite, Telegram et BitChat : comment les manifestants s’organisent pour l’acte II du 24 octobre

En prévision ou pour s'organiser en marge des manifestations du samedi 24 octobre, les choses s'organisent avec une carte collaborative, des canaux Telegram, Signal, et même BitChat. On a listé les outils numériques qui circulent.
À la veille des manifestations du 24 octobre, l'« acte II » de la mobilisation contre la vie chère s'organise autant sur les téléphones et sur les réseaux sociaux, que sur le pavé, sans mauvais jeu de mots. Une carte collaborative recense par exemple déjà plus de 660 rendez-vous, des messageries chiffrées font office de QG et trois médias ont même ouvert une ligne pour recueillir les images de violences policières. Mais entre les arrêtés préfectoraux en cascade, les recours devant les tribunaux pour faire autoriser des rassemblements interdits par les préfets, comme à Marseille, et les contrôles annoncés dans les gares, mieux vaut savoir ce que ces outils montrent… et ce qu'ils passent sous silence.
Cette carte des manifestations du 24 octobre est complète, sauf qu'elle ne dit pas où il est interdit de défiler

articles.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide
Most fine-tuning teaches a model to produce a better answer to a single prompt. Agentic tasks are different. An agent that files an expense report or triages a support ticket takes a sequence of actions, and each step depends on what came before. There’s rarely one correct sequence to imitate, and the only reliable feedback is whether the whole sequence succeeded. Supervised fine-tuning has no labels for that, and single-turn reinforcement learning cannot credit a decision made three steps before the outcome.
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on exactly that signal. SageMaker AI sends prompts to an agent you host on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, or on your own infrastructure, such as Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), or AWS Fargate, through an AWS Lambda forwarder. The example here uses AgentCore. The agent calls the policy model being trained, acts in your environment over as many turns as the task needs, and reports one reward when the episode ends. You don’t specify the right trajectory, only how to score the result.
This post uses Wordle, a game in which a player has six tries to guess a hidden five-letter word, as the example. After each guess, every letter turns green if it is in the right position, yellow if it’s in the word but in a different position, and gray if it isn’t in…

Thanks to a newly developed, vibe-coded emulator, some games in the console's library can now be played with limited color, reportedly added through a hand-painted process.
Despite selling just 770,000 units worldwide, Nintendo's Virtual Boy still has a small but dedicated fan base experimenting with new ways to use the console. The stereoscopic system failed to achieve commercial success and could display games only in monochrome red hues. Now, a new emulator called VBoy Color aims to change that by introducing limited color to Virtual Boy games on desktop computers and in virtual reality (VR).
According to VBoy Color's GitHub page, the open-source emulator adds colors to areas that would otherwise appear in different shades of red on the original system. It uses a tile-based approach in which each 8×8-pixel tile is assigned a color from a four-color palette. This technique can reportedly give pipes, platforms, bricks, and classic Nintendo characters distinct color schemes.
Colorization could make games such as Jack Bros. and Vertical Force more visually appealing than they are on the Virtual Boy's original monochrome display. The project could also renew interest in Nintendo's ill-fated console, particularly now that the company has released a new accessory for playing Virtual Boy games on modern Switch systems.

Oppo vient de lancer ses Find X10 et Find X10 Pro Max le 21 octobre. Deux appareils à plus de 1000 euros et dont le plus cher taquine même les 2000 euros. À 1800 euros, le Find X10 Pro Max est très proche d’un iPhone 18 Pro Max à stockage égal.
Face à l’inflation générale du secteur, le PDG Europe d’Oppo, Elvis Zahou, rejette les compromis techniques : « OPPO n’a pas fait le choix de certaines marques qui sortent une nouvelle génération sans véritable mise à jour matérielle ou logicielle, voire en réduisant certaines configurations pour limiter la hausse des prix ». « Face à la hausse des coûts, chaque nouvelle génération que nous sortons doit impérativement apporter une amélioration majeure de l’expérience par rapport à la précédente […]. Sur le haut de gamme, Oppo vise les 18-35 ans, et en particulier la Gen Z. D’après une étude interne citée par Elvis Zahou, PDG Europe d’Oppo, cette tranche d’âge représente plus de la moitié des utilisateurs de smartphones haut de gamme. Oppo a identifié trois attentes de ce public : la photo, l’intelligence artificielle et le bien-être. Pour Oppo, la série Find doit combler leurs attentes.

Après avoir augmenté le tarif de ses consoles, Microsoft se lance maintenant dans une nouvelle opération commerciale, un mail à ses utilisateurs de Xbox. Ce dernier invite clairement les utilisateurs à se débarrasser de leur console, en la revendant. Pourquoi une telle démarche ? Microsoft semble surtout admettre qu'ils n'auront pas de consoles pour tout le monde.
Un message adressé aux consoles inactives
Sur X, un utilisateur sous le nom Nintendeal a partagé le contenu d'un mail reçu de Microsoft. Le message cible spécifiquement les possesseurs de Xbox Series X ou Series S qui n'ont pas utilisé leur console depuis un certain temps.
Vous n'avez pas joué sur votre console depuis un moment ? Si vous êtes passé à Xbox sur PC ou à une autre façon de jouer aux jeux Xbox, il est peut-être temps d'échanger votre console chez Best Buy (revendeur américain) pour récupérer jusqu'à 375 dollars. - Dit le message de Microsoft

articles.title: Deepseek's latest AI model is smarter than ever, but its low running costs come at a price — uses only one-quarter of the HBM and one-eighth of SSD storage but still battles hallucinations in agentic workloads
articles.summary:
Deepseek's latest AI model is smarter than ever, but its low running costs come at a price — uses only one-quarter of the HBM and one-eighth of SSD storage but still battles hallucinations in agentic workloads
Frontier models are far more capable but paying a premium is quickly becoming a matter of choice
Deepseek just upgraded its V4.1 Flash open-weight model to revision 1017. What looks like a mere point revision may actually be a significant step forward in model efficiency. On the product page, Deepseek uses the slogan "wish-driven programming made real," a likely reference to the colloquial "vibe coding," implying the model is a good fit for open-ended tasks with broad descriptions. However, while the model is indeed cheap and scores well, it can be hallucination-prone.
LLMs are roughly divided into two categories: closed commercial efforts from frontier labs, whose models are expensive to run but deliver excellent results, and Chinese open-weight competitors that broadly exchange reliability for a much cheaper running cost, particularly for long-running agentic tasks.
Deepseek V4.1 Flash (DSF) is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B total parameters, 16B of which are active during runs. The model is multimodal, accepts both text and images as inputs, and its context window length measures the now-standard 1 million tokens.
According to Deepseek's internal benchmarks, the model slots in neatly between GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5, even beating Anthropic's LLM in t…

articles.title: Inside the Pentagon, the pressure is on to find a home for a new spaceport
articles.summary:
Leaders in the US Space Force would like to have a new spaceport up and running in four years, adding a third heavy-lift launch site to relieve pressure from bases in Florida and California that have shot rockets into orbit for nearly 70 years.
The obvious problem with that ambition is 2030 is four years away, and Pentagon officials have not determined where the new spaceport should go or how to acquire land for it.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink first mentioned the service’s search for a third launch base in May. A congressionally mandated study of the Space Force’s launch infrastructure identified the need for “another site that’s capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability,” Meink said in a House Armed Services Committee hearing.
The Trump administration released a space transportation policy in August that endorsed the construction of more launch and reentry sites for commercial and military missions. This week, the Space Force general responsible for procuring launch services for the military laid out an “aspirational” timeline for a new launch site.
“We need this capability by 2030, but I’m also a pragmatist,” said Lt. Gen. Philip Garrant, head of Space Systems Command. “That is not an inconsequential demand to build a spaceport when you factor in orbital regimes, safety, access to commodities, the Americans that live near it. In many ways, it’s much like an airport, but even louder. So there’s a lot of consideration.”

articles.title: Ontario to start consultations on developing digital IDs
articles.summary:
The Ontario government is taking the first steps toward introducing digital identification cards, which will give residents the option of keeping their official credentials on their phones instead of relying solely on physical cards.
Keeping your digital credentials on your phone would be completely optional under the proposed changes, which would include permanently guaranteeing that Ontario residents can maintain access to their physical ID cards.
“As we modernize government services, we’re making identification more secure, convenient and cost-effective,” said Minister of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement, Stephen Crawford.
“Digital credentials will provide a trusted and seamless way to present identification, helping protect personal information while retaining every Ontario resident’s right to use physical I.D.”
The province says digital credentials would support a more seamless customer experience while also providing an added layer of security by reducing the risk of lost or stolen identification. Those with digital credentials would be able to store their ID on their mobile devices and use them to access services in person or online.
Starting later this year, the provincial government is set to begin consultations that will help shape the development of digital credentials. articles.title: New Fan Project Brings Xbox One Games to iPhone Without Emulating the Hardware
articles.summary:
Friday, October 23rd 2026
New Fan Project Brings Xbox One Games to iPhone Without Emulating the Hardware
A developer who goes by levi on X has announced Utsuro, a new project that runs Xbox One games on Apple devices. It's still very early, but the developer says it already runs Minecraft: Xbox One Edition "extremely well," and the attached video shows it running on iOS with touchscreen controls. According to the project's GitHub page, Minecraft hits around 36 to 60 FPS on the Mac build, and Sonic Mania and Rocket League run there too, complete with screenshots. Sonic Mania is marked as playable at around 57 FPS with sound, while Rocket League renders and drives at roughly 15 to 20 FPS, with dark lighting and no audio yet.
Utsuro also works differently from a typical emulator. Apparently, it skips hardware emulation altogether and runs the console's Windows-based software layer as x86-64 code on Apple's Arm chips through FEXCore, and fills in the system pieces the console itself would normally provide. Graphics go through Apple's Metal API, with the Xbox One's Direct3D 11.X shaders converted to Metal's shader language, while audio runs on CoreAudio. Getting it running isn't exactly simple either. On iOS, the app has to be sideloaded, needs a JIT helper like StikDebug, TrollStore, or a jailbroken device, and expects a decrypted dump of the game. articles.title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
On Wednesday, a decades-old open-source web technology called PHP almost broke the internet, thanks to two vulnerabilities that had sat dormant for years until researchers recently figured out a way to exploit them.
The bugs are dubbed PHP2Shell, officially designated as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. In simple terms, the bugs allow anyone who knows how to exploit them to break into an online system running PHP, such as a website or internet-facing server, without needing a password to access or modify its data.
As situations go, this was a pretty sizable one, forcing millions of people around the world to scramble to patch their systems before malicious hackers could abuse them.
The PHP Foundation, which maintains the PHP web software, publicly released patches on Wednesday that fixed the bugs, which when installed prevent web-facing servers from being attacked. The foundation had already given some of the biggest internet companies and web hosts that rely on PHP an early headstart on patching.
Thanks to weeks of backroom chatter and careful coordination across the industry, the world — so far — broadly avoided mass internet exploitation. From Wednesday, governments began urging citizens and companies with websites to take action to mitigate the risks on their ends. A wide range of industries shuttered their websites and pulled services offline to patch their systems. La operación tendría consecuencias directas sobre los acuerdos que vinculan la remuneración de Musk con el desempeño financiero de sus empresas. Entre ellas figura una cláusula que permitiría liberar acciones restringidas de Tesla antes de la fecha prevista originalmente.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo's screen is cracking in the same weird L-shape for multiple owners
articles.summary:
Cutting corners: When Apple unveiled the foldable Duo, many wondered how well the hinge and screen would hold up. Within hours of the iPhone Duo's launch, images of cracked screens began circulating on social media, and the damage isn't limited to the fold itself.
The iPhone Duo subreddit alone already has multiple threads from users complaining about, and sharing pictures of, cracked screens. Some report that Apple has been generous with replacements for the $2,000 phone so far, but it remains to be seen how the company's policy will evolve as it works through production challenges.
Most of the photos show a break running along the fold, with a bright line of pixels extending from it toward the right edge of the screen. The result resembles a giant white L-shape stretching from one end of the internal screen to the middle.
iPhone Duo screen cracked within 6 hours of ownership
by u/Midnight_Slump in iPhoneDuo
One user in Australia reported the problem just six hours after buying the iPhone Duo, having opened the device fewer than 20 times. He says he felt something along the hinge beneath the screen before hearing a crack as the display broke. There were no marks on the screen's surface or the exterior hinge to suggest anything had been caught.
Apple's phone support offered an express replacement but required a hold for the phone's full price, and couldn't say when the replacement would arrive. He went to the Apple Store instead, where staff immediately granted a full replace…

articles.title: En Galicia hay casas de piedra por 10.000 euros y pueblos que ofrecen exenciones fiscales. Pero no buscan compradores
articles.summary:
Hay quien busca casa en el pueblo para jubilarse y quien, quizá hasta las narices del frenesí urbano, quiere montar allí una bodega, una panadería o un albergue y vivir a otro ritmo. Para los segundos existe Holapueblo, una web que pone en contacto a emprendedores con concellos que necesitan que alguien reabra el negocio que cerró. Tres municipios ourensanos acaban de apuntarse, según Faro de Vigo: Chandrexa de Queixa, Castrelo de Miño y Beariz. Su argumento común es que sobra espacio y tranquilidad.
Qué es Holapueblo. Una plataforma que impulsan Redeia, IKEA y AlmaNatura. Ofrece asesoramiento personalizado para encontrar vivienda y poner en marcha el proyecto, con ayudas autonómicas y locales. Son ese gestor que aclara dudas y funciona más como ventanilla que como sorteo de casas.
Chandrexa de Queixa. Con 985 metros, es el concello más alto de la provincia. Tiene 467 vecinos (de 478 que tenía hace solo un año) repartidos en 172 kilómetros cuadrados: 2,7 habitantes por kilómetro cuadrado. Su economía es ganadera, con más de 1.300 cabezas de vacuno y 3.500 de ovino, y ofrece pastos comunales e incentivos específicos a nuevos ganaderos o apicultores.
También se vende como oportunidad turística: la estación de Manzaneda está a 15 minutos, la Ribeira Sacra a 30 y la oferta de alojamiento se reduce a viviendas turísticas aisladas. articles.title: La lutte française contre l'IPTV pirate pointée du doigt dans un nouveau rapport international
articles.summary:
Les décisions françaises obligeant des fournisseurs de VPN à bloquer des sites pirates se retrouvent dans un nouveau rapport international. Une coalition d'entreprises du numérique alerte sur les conséquences possibles de cette stratégie, alors que les États-Unis débattent à leur tour des obligations à imposer à ces intermédiaires.
D'abord les fournisseurs d'accès, puis les résolveurs DNS et désormais les VPN. Comme vous le savez, en France, la lutte contre le piratage sportif s'est progressivement étendue à de nouveaux intermédiaires techniques. Une évolution désormais citée dans un rapport publié le 21 octobre par l'Internet Infrastructure Coalition (i2Coalition), qui s'interroge sur les limites de cette stratégie.
Pourquoi les blocages français inquiètent la coalition
Intitulé VPNs at Risk, le rapport examine les restrictions imposées aux VPN dans sept pays, dont la France, l'Inde, le Pakistan et la Russie. Il émane d'une organisation professionnelle représentant notamment des fournisseurs de VPN, dont elle défend aussi les intérêts.
En France, le document cite les procédures engagées par Canal+ contre NordVPN, Surfshark, CyberGhost, ExpressVPN et Proton VPN. Elles s'appuient sur l'article L.333-10 du Code du sport, issu de la loi de 2021, qui permet d'imposer des mesures de blocage à des intermédiaires susceptibles de contribuer à faire cesser le piratage sportif.

articles.summary:
FCC issues first bans under new chip-level rule — dashcam and video transmitter carried Huawei AI silicon with face tracking
Huawei subsidiary's surveillance products get banned over AI chip in SoC.
The FCC recently imposed a new rule allowing it to ban devices based on the internal chips instead of basing bans on individual products or brands, thus closing the loophole of rebranded products with parts from Chinese manufacturers on US export restriction lists. Using this new rule, the FCC has banned two devices from being sold and marketed in the US for the first time: a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter. As reported by The Verge, these devices were banned due to the HiSilicon Smart Vision SoC (System on a Chip) they contain, which features built-in detection algorithms for faces. HiSilicon is a subsidiary of Huawei, and the firm and its subsidiaries are on the FCC’s Covered List of entities that pose a risk to US national security.
The Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision is an SoC for surveillance and camera products. The SoC is meant to be used for things like vehicle dashcams and wireless CCTV systems; fully equipped with WiFi, Ethernet, video encoding chips, an Arm Cortex-A7, and an NPU (Neural Processing Unit) for AI features. The NPU is what the FCC is concerned about, explaining that it is a device that contains logic-bearing “smart” components produced by entities on the Covered List.

articles.title: « On va me haïr » : cette romancière a écrit 371 livres grâce à ChatGPT, Claude et Grok, et elle assume
articles.summary:
Thélyson Orélien a finalement admis « qu’une partie du processus d’écriture [du roman C’était ça ou mourir] a reposé sur l’IA ». Coral Hart, elle, assume pleinement avoir recours à l’IA pour écrire ses romans, comme elle l’explique à l’AFP. En fait, cette quadragénaire sud-africaine en a fait un véritable business. Elle propose même de générer des romans à votre place : 260 $ pour un livre unique et 705 $ pour une trilogie.
Près de 400 romans écrits à l’aide de l’IA en moins de 2 ans
En l’espace de 20 mois, Coral Hart a écrit, ou plutôt généré, 371 romans à l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle. Un chiffre qui donnerait certainement le tournis à George R. R. Martin, l’auteur de Game of Thrones. Le processus de travail de Coral Hart est relativement simple. Tout d’abord, elle établit les grandes lignes de l’histoire, les personnages ou encore la structure globale du livre. Ensuite, elle fournit ces indications à une IA qui délivre un texte. Cependant, Coral Hart explique que la première version est systématiquement « mauvaise ». C’est pourquoi elle demande à une autre IA d’harmoniser l’ensemble notamment la continuité du récit et la cohérence globale. Enfin, un relecteur humain s’assure que l’IA n’a pas laissé d’erreur ou d’incohérence. Il peut même réécrire certains passages s’il le faut.
La romancière explique par ailleurs jongler avec différentes IA. ChatGPT serait ainsi « très bon sur les dialogues », Claude « incroyable pour la prose » et Grok « totalement désinhibé », et…

articles.title: 5 Lessons to learn from Nexus by Yuval Noah Harari
articles.summary:
5 Lessons to learn from Nexus by Yuval Noah Harari
Discover five key lessons from Yuval Noah Harari’s Nexus on information, power, artificial intelligence and how networks shape society.
Information has always shaped human civilisation. From ancient stories and religious texts to newspapers, television and social media, the way people share information influences what they believe, how they make decisions and whom they trust.
In Nexus, historian and author Yuval Noah Harari examines how information networks have shaped human history and how they may influence our future. Published in 2024, the book explores the relationship between information, power, truth and the development of artificial intelligence.
Harari challenges the assumption that having more information automatically makes societies wiser or better informed.
What matters is how information is organised, who controls it and whether the systems that distribute it help people correct their mistakes. Here are five important lessons to learn from Nexus and how they apply to the world we live in today.

1. More information does not always mean more truth

AI data centres are projected to consume 70% of global memory chip production in 2026. The data centre boom has led to a supply crunch, subsequently shoring up costs of chips.

Hegseth wrote:
Our enemies watch movements in these markets. When an American Service member, intelligence professional, or other Department civilian engages in a financial transaction on a military outcome, they create a signal. That signal can be aggregated, correlated, and exploited by hostile foreign intelligence services to anticipate our movements, targets, and timing. The lives of our Service members often depend on the enemy not knowing what is coming. The men and women who carry our flag into harm’s way deserve a Force that protects them—not one that exposes them to the enemy for personal gain.

Although much of the information behind these plans has been previously reported at Ars Technica and elsewhere, this marked the first time NASA has laid them out in detail and acknowledged some substantial changes in the architecture.
Most notably, for SpaceX’s Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. And for Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings. Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allows for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit.
During the presentation on Friday, NASA officials said they continue to anticipate launching the Artemis III mission—a demonstration involving docking with both Blue Moon and Starship near Earth—by “summer” 2027. And they are still tracking toward a 2028 launch of Artemis IV, which would involve an actual landing on the lunar surface.
“This is an achievable path we are on right now,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said. “We have the mandate, we have the resources, and the support from our stakeholders to be able to execute, and that’s what we intend to do.”

Amazon is allegedly taking in billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia racks every month, even though some sites aren't ready for them and there is no electricity to feed the AI accelerators just yet. According to internal emails seen by Business Insider, Amazon is willing to tie up billions in cash upfront as long as it can secure new hardware capacity early.
The messages describe Amazon's Early Rack Receipt process, through which AWS expected to take around $5 billion worth of Nvidia GB300 server racks in August alone, with roughly $3 billion more expected every month for the foreseeable future. Amazon is getting servers "built for the age of AI reasoning" before the final deployment phase.
Some US-based AWS facilities don't have enough power to install and turn the servers on, which means the costly hardware is being stored in "intermediary" warehouses until the final data center site is completed. In the emails, one Amazon team lamented that there was no clear forecast for actually installing all the GPUs the company was acquiring each month.

articles.title: Ice sheet expansion may have started 2,000 years ago, but we canceled that
articles.summary:
Barnes Ice Cap sits on the central plateau of Baffin Island, in the Canadian Arctic. It is the last surviving fragment of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, which at its peak buried most of Canada under two miles of ice and locked away around 80 meters of sea level. That remnant has now yielded direct physical evidence that ice sheets might have reversed their retreat and started to grow again thousands of years ago.
In a recent Science study, researchers show that the Laurentide reached its smallest size about 3,600 years ago, then started re-expanding roughly 2,000 years ago, which the team interprets as the opening move of the next glaciation. Apparently, this brand-new ice age was on its way until about 1960, when human-caused climate warming reversed it.
Frozen to the bed
“Barnes is the last remaining piece of one of the domes of the Laurentide Ice Sheet,” says Nicolás Young, a geologist at Columbia University’s Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory and lead author of the study. As that enormous dome thinned through the Holocene, its margin withdrew up onto Baffin Island, and what’s left today is the deflated core of something that was once two miles thick. The reason Barnes can testify about its own history, Young explains, comes down to the temperature at its base.
Most glaciers are warm-based, meaning meltwater at the bed lets them slide, and sliding ice grinds up everything beneath it, erasing the record. Barnes is cold-based, and thus fr…

articles.title: Holzalkohol im Weltraum entdeckt: Was das für Planetenforschung bedeutet
articles.summary:
Holzalkohol im All: Forscher entdecken „schweres Methanol“ 1.000 Lichtjahre entfernt
Holzalkohol ist in der Industrie von großer Bedeutung. Die klare, farblose und leicht flüchtige Flüssigkeit ist ein wichtiger Grundstoff zur Herstellung von Kunststoffen, Formaldehyd, Essigsäure und Farben. Außerdem ist er auch ein Bestandteil von Frostschutzmitteln.
Holzalkohol spielt als organisches Molekül auch eine wesentliche Rolle bei der Bildung komplexer organischer Moleküle im Weltraum. Im Rahmen des „ALMA COMPASS“-Forschungsprogramms wurde nun vollständig deuteriertes Methanol, sogenanntes „schweres Methanol“ (CD3OD), in der Umgebung des Protosterns IRAS4A2 nachgewiesen. Forscher:innen des Max Planck Instituts in Garching sind besonders neugierig, da sie sich die dort beobachtete Menge nicht erklären können.
These: Moleküle reagieren bereits vor der Stern-Entstehung
Wissenschaftler:innen haben bereits Hinweise auf weitere komplexe Moleküle, etwa Isopropanol, das als Reinigungsalkohol bekannt ist, in der Umgebung sehr junger Sternsysteme gefunden. Experimente deuten darauf hin, dass diese Moleküle wahrscheinlich auf der Oberfläche eisiger Staubkörner in kalten Nebelwolken entstehen.
Dort reagieren sie langsam mit Kohlenstoff, Sauerstoff, Wasserstoff und anderen Atomen zu immer komplexeren Verbindungen – und das lange, bevor ein neuer Stern überhaupt entsteht. Sobald der Protostern zu leuchten beginnt und seine Umgebung erwärmt, werden diese Verbindungen laut Universe Today freigesetz…

articles.title: China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing
articles.summary:
China can make advanced chips without EUV, but the bill keeps growing — DUV multiple patterning means bigger dies, lower yields, and longer manufacturing times
China has shown that older DUV lithography can be stretched much further than many expected – but can it fully catch up?
Export controls have kept ASML's most advanced EUV lithography machines out of China. Instead, the country's chipmaking industry has relied on less-capable deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines. By using multiple exposures on critical chip layers, these older machines are still capable of producing performant silicon. However, as multiple patterns are applied there are more chances for defects, longer manufacturing times, and higher bills. We spoke to experts like Chris Mack, co-founder and CTO of semiconductor firm Fractilia, to find out how much further DUV can go.
For years, extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography has been seen as China’s biggest choke point in the country’s attempts to build cutting-edge chips. The machines, made exclusively by Dutch manufacturer ASML, use 13.5nm-wavelength light to print some of the most intricate features found on modern processors. Sales of ASML’s EUV systems are subject to export restrictions, forcing Chinese manufacturers to squeeze ever more out of older deep ultraviolet, or DUV, lithography instead. The EUV gap alone between China and the West is at least half a decade, according to some analysts.

articles.title: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
articles.summary:
Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.
Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet’s atmosphere.
“We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before,” Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release. “Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”

articles.title: MapQuest adds surveillance camera locations in Canada
articles.summary:
MapQuest returned to the cultural zeitgeist earlier this year when it rejected U.S. President Donald Trump’s push to rename Lake Ontario. Now it’s making headlines for displaying the location of surveillance cameras, at the request of users.
MapQuest now has a ‘surveillance layer’ that users can enable, which displays an animated eye where there are automated licence plate readers (ALPRs).
The move comes amid increasing scrutiny of cameras like ALPRs, which some consider a growing privacy concern. While police view these cameras as tools for finding criminals, stolen vehicles, missing people, and more, the public has valid concerns about misuse.
This is particularly true in the U.S., where ALPRs from companies like Flock are increasingly being used for predatory behaviour, from pulling over innocent people to stalking people and recording children. And that’s not even getting into how the White House is leveraging these cameras for widespread surveillance.
Per CBC News, MapQuest’s camera markers include Flock cameras as well as those from other companies, including Genetec, PlateSmart, Neology, and Verkada. Additionally, the camera locations come from crowd-sourced data from OpenStreetMap.
Of course, MapQuest isn’t the only one mapping these cameras. Several other tools have cropped up for mapping ALPRs from Flock and other companies. There’s panopti.ca, a Canada-focused, open-source ALPR mapping tool, which is built on top of DeFlock, a similar tool for the US. Another simil…

articles.title: Intel obtuvo una excepción para seguir usando robots extranjeros en sus plantas de chips en Estados Unidos
articles.summary:
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de Estados Unidos le otorgó a Intel una excepción por un año para que la fabricante de chips siga usando robots fabricados en el extranjero dentro de sus plantas, pese a una nueva prohibición federal sobre este tipo de dispositivos.
La agencia, conocida como FCC, publicó la orden el 22 de octubre de 2026 tras una solicitud de Intel presentada apenas seis días antes, el 16. La compañía pidió la excepción “por pura precaución”, ya que no tenía certeza de si sus vehículos quedaban alcanzados por la nueva norma.
Los equipos en cuestión son vehículos guiados automáticamente que se desplazan sobre rieles o rutas predefinidas, casi siempre bajo la supervisión de un operador humano y que Intel utiliza para trasladar materiales dentro de sus fábricas de semiconductores.
Según Bloomberg News, este tipo de vehículos suele ser fabricado por empresas japonesas como Murata Machinery y Daifuku. Intel no reveló qué modelos específicos utiliza: esa información quedó en un anexo confidencial que acompañó su pedido ante la FCC.
Parte de esas fábricas, como la planta Fab 52 en Chandler, Arizona, son centrales en la apuesta de Intel por recuperar terreno en la manufactura de chips avanzados frente a rivales como TSMC y Samsung.
La excepción otorgada a Intel vence en octubre de 2027, cuando la compañía deberá demostrar ante la FCC si consiguió reemplazar sus vehículos importados por equipos fabricados en Estados Unidos o si necesitará una nueva prórroga para m…

articles.title: How to avoid AI's 'valley of despair' - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
How to avoid AI’s ‘valley of despair’
Amdahl’s Law states that improving a single part of a system can only speed up the whole system so much. Even if one step of a process becomes exponentially faster, the other steps impose a ceiling unless they, too, are accelerated.
This concept may explain some of the disappointment companies are experiencing with artificial intelligence. An AI assistant can draft a proposal in seconds, but it then sits for days waiting on reviews, pricing and approval. Similarly, a coding tool can produce software in minutes, but testing, security and deployment still take days or weeks.
Companies have accelerated specific tasks without reengineering the systems that surround them. This gap between inflated expectations and modest returns is what some are calling AI’s “valley of despair.”
After a period of vigorous adoption and experimentation, executives are now being confronted with ever-growing costs and limited proof of bottom-line impact. Analyst firm Forrester Research Inc. recently found that only 15% of AI decision-makers reported an increase in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization over the past 12 months. Fewer than one-third could clearly map the value of AI back to bottom-line changes.
This skepticism is healthy; AI investments should face the same scrutiny as any other capital expense. Leaders need to be clear on expected returns, timelines and milestones that show whether their investment delivers measurable busine…

articles.title: "No hay esperanza para los glaciares del Pirineo". Las fotos del Aneto tras el verano sugieren un colapso climático extremo
articles.summary:
El cambio climático está agravando la desertificación de España y, en el proceso, desestabilizando brutalmente el caudal de los ríos y haciendo que los Pirineos sean más mediterráneos que nunca. Y eso implica también decir adiós a uno de los pocos glaciares que hay en la península Ibérica: el del Aneto. Como una imagen vale más que mil palabras, bajo estas líneas verás dos fotografías del Aneto, de 2015 y 2026. El cambio es evidente: donde antes había un cuerpo blanco de nieve y hielo, ahora domina la roca desnuda y el hielo sucio.
La agonía del Aneto. La descorazonadora imagen que muestran las dos fotografías no debería pillarnos por sorpresa. El grupo CryoPyr del Instituto Pirenaico de Ecología (IPE-CSIC) lleva años midiendo su retroceso con drones y láser y, tras su campaña de septiembre de 2025, detalló que el cuerpo principal se fragmentó bajo el Pico del Medio y que la masa bajo el Collado de Coronas pasó a considerarse un helero. El resultado son tres masas de hielo desconectadas, un estado muy distinto al de 2015.
Los resultados preliminares de la campaña de final de este verano apuntan a una pérdida de más de dos metros de espesor medio, que deja el grosor medio del glaciar en torno a los 12 metros. El investigador Ignacio López-Moreno, del IPE-CSIC, recuerda que durante las últimas dos décadas la pérdida rondaba un metro al año, aunque en 2022 y 2023 superó los tres.

articles.title: Cet appareil pourrait mettre votre robinet au chomage

Hurom lance un purificateur d'eau qui filtre, chauffe et refroidit
Trois filtres et l'addition
On connait la marque pour ses extracteurs de jus, Hurom s'intéresse désormais à l'eau. Son premier purificateur associe filtration par osmose inverse, chauffage et refroidissement dans un appareil à poser sur le plan de travail.
Après avoir séparé le jus de la pulpe, Hurom veut retenir ce qui se trouve dans l'eau. La marque a dévoilé le WP-A01EGR, un purificateur doté d'un réservoir de 8,5 l, capable de distribuer de l'eau filtrée, chaude ou froide. Il réunit plusieurs usages pour remplir un verre, préparer un thé ou disposer d'eau chaude pour toute autre préparation.
Trois filtres au passage
La filtration repose sur trois étapes. Un premier filtre à charbon actif en poudre, baptisé PAC, vise à réduire le chlore, les odeurs et certains composés organiques. L'eau traverse ensuite une membrane d'osmose inverse, chargée de retenir notamment les métaux lourds, les bactéries, les virus et les particules microscopiques. Un dernier bloc de charbon actif, nommé CF, complète le traitement et doit améliorer le goût de l'eau.
Le panneau tactile permet de régler la température par pas de 1 °C. Le refroidissement repose sur un compresseur. Les débits dépendent de l'usage : 30 l/h pour l'eau filtrée, 18 l/h pour l'eau chaude et 0,8 l/h pour l'eau froide. Attention, donc, si toute la famille compte enchaîner les verres d'eau fraîche. That volatility isn’t likely to change anytime soon, as more big earnings reports are coming next week, including the major cloud and AI providers Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft as well as Intel. Eso, justamente, es lo que parece que está ocurriendo con “El nacimiento de Venus”. Y es que, además de ser una de las obras más emblemáticas del Quattrocento italiano, parece que este cuadro de Sandro Botticelli encierra también una posible prueba de cuál fue la causa de la muerte de la enigmática Simonetta Vespucci.
Casada con solo 16 años con el noble Marco Vespucci, Simonetta se hizo pronto de una gran fama entre la élite florentina, tanto a causa de su belleza como de su intelecto. Uno de los muchos hombres que se prendaron de ella fue el propio Botticelli, quien no tardó en convertirla en su musa. No hay una cifra definitiva de cuadros en los que aparece su rostro, ya que no solo se encuentra en retratos, sino que sus rasgos sirvieron como inspiración para ninfas y otros personajes femeninos de la obra del pintor. Sin embargo, han sido cinco cuadros en concreto los que han llevado a un equipo de científicos italianos a averiguar que, posiblemente, la joven padecía un tumor neuroendocrino de la hipófisis.
Una muerte misteriosa. Simonetta falleció en 1476, a los 23 años, después de un baile. Según las cartas que envió su suegro, Piero Vespucci, a Lorenzo de Medici, se derrumbó mientras bailaba y tuvo que pasar varios días en cama, durante los cuales sufrió fuertes dolores de cabeza, mareos, alucinaciones y vómitos. Un gendarme mondial, une fusion ou un seul vainqueur
Le premier scénario décrit la création d’un organisme international chargé d’encadrer les modèles les plus puissants, à la manière de ce qui existe pour le nucléaire. Les États y fixeraient ensemble des limites que les laboratoires ne pourraient plus franchir seuls. Une piste qu’Altman défend de longue date : dès 2023, il plaidait publiquement pour une agence internationale dédiée, inspirée de celle qui surveille l’atome. Le deuxième verrait les grands acteurs du secteur se regrouper, à terme, en une seule entité, et la compétition s’éteindre par concentration.
Le troisième scénario repose sur l’auto-amélioration récursive, cette capacité d’une IA à perfectionner elle-même les modèles qui lui succèdent, chaque génération accélérant la conception de la suivante. La perspective n’a rien de théorique : dès juin 2025, Altman décrivait une « version larvaire » de ce mécanisme, les chercheurs utilisant déjà l’IA pour accélérer leurs propres travaux. El hallazgo. Lo que el agricultor encontró fue un bloque de piedra rosa cubierto de jeroglíficos.
Tras el aviso, la excavación de rescate sacó a la luz los restos de dos enormes estatuas. La primera es una cabeza de Ramsés II de 1,6 metros. También apareció buena parte de una segunda estatua real, de unos 2,4 metros. Capcom has confirmed that an unauthorized third party accessed customer data tied to CAPCOM ID, the shared account used for the company's web services and for online play in some of its games. According to Capcom's official notice, a massive 11,774,247 records were affected worldwide, each containing an email address along with the account creation date, last login time, login count, and the IP address from the most recent sign-in. Capcom spotted the suspicious activity on October 19, started blocking it the same day, and reported the incident to the Osaka Prefectural Police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on October 21. A much smaller group of 43 records also exposed dates of birth, gender, country or region, and nicknames. 
The attackers changed the login passwords on 196 accounts too, and Capcom has since reset them. A follow-up notice on October 23 adds that the intruder opened the e-Capcom store pages of 19 of those accounts, exposing names, phone numbers, addresses, and purchase history for those customers in Japan. Capcom says it found no sign that customer-set passwords were compromised, and credit card information was not affected. Capcom hasn't said how the attackers got in, only that the method has been identified and dealt with. CAPCOM ID and Capcom's games remain available. Los fabricantes de chips y los desarrolladores de servidores figuran entre los principales beneficiados del auge de infraestructura para IA, en particular en Estados Unidos, de acuerdo con el informe de BofA.

Y pese a que lo hayamos visto tanto, especialmente en el noroeste de la península, que lo sentimos de toda la vida, a la acacia le pasa como al ailanto: es una especie exótica invasora en España (salvo Canarias y Baleares).
Las presentaciones. Aunque sus flores y su olor son lo suficientemente característicos como para reconocerla, la mimosa es un árbol que puede llegar a los 15 metros de altura y de hoja perenne. Su corteza es gris o blanquecina, muy lista y con mucha ramificación. Las hojas son doblemente pinadas y produce una vaina aplastada y curva que contiene entre cuatro y cinco semillas. En las fases iniciales no soporta la sombra y las heladas no le sientan nada bien, de ahí que prospere en aquellas zonas con clima suave.
Cómo llegó hasta aquí. articles.title: Faut-il laisser son PC portable branché au secteur en permanence ? La vérité sur l'usure des batteries

Faut-il laisser son PC portable branché au secteur en permanence ? La vérité sur l'usure des batteries
Laisser son ordinateur portable branché toute la journée use-t-il sa batterie ? Oui et non. Ce qui fatigue les cellules, c'est de rester des heures à 100 %, et plus encore dans une machine qui chauffe. Les Mac compatibles permettent désormais de fixer une limite de charge dans les réglages. Sur PC Windows, la fonction existe souvent aussi, mais il faut la chercher dans l'utilitaire du constructeur.
Prenez un portable resté deux ans sur un bureau, branché du matin au soir à un écran externe. Il n'a quasiment jamais tourné sur batterie. Le jour où on le débranche pour une réunion, mauvaise surprise : l'autonomie a nettement baissé, et l'outil de diagnostic affiche une capacité tombée à 70 % de sa valeur d'origine. Deux ans sans servir, 30 % de perdus. Comment est-ce possible ?
Une batterie vieillit aussi au repos
Écartons une vieille peur. Un portable moderne ne "surcharge" pas sa batterie : une fois pleine, son circuit de gestion coupe la charge et le chargeur cesse d'alimenter les cellules. Ce mécanisme fonctionne très bien. Le problème se voit moins. Une batterie lithium-ion s'use de deux manières. La première, tout le monde la connaît : chaque cycle de charge et de décharge l'abîme un peu, c'est le vieillissement cyclique. The gfx117x IDs belong to RDNA 4m, which first showed up in LLVM back in February. AMD added GFX1171 and GFX1172 targets in March, merged GFX1171 into Mesa 26.3 in August, and pushed RDNA 4m firmware later that month. Despite the name, RDNA 4m sits in the GFX11 family with RDNA 3 and 3.5, plus a few RDNA 4 style additions like FP8/BF8 conversion and new matrix instructions. The gfx115E entry is the more curious one. GFX115x covers the RDNA 3.5 graphics in Strix Point and Strix Halo, so it looks like at least one Medusa chip could stick with RDNA 3.5. articles.title: Esta es la contaminación oculta que genera una impresión láser: equivaldría a 20 mil millones de plásticos al año
articles.summary:
20 mil millones de bolsas plásticas al año: esa es la equivalencia de los residuos que generan los insumos de impresión láser a nivel global, según cálculos presentados por la industria. Detrás de una hoja impresa hay un proceso que utiliza polvo plástico, calor y componentes que deben reemplazarse con frecuencia.
Las impresoras láser funcionan con tóner, un cartucho que contiene un polvo fino con micropartículas plásticas.
Ese material no se deposita sobre el papel como una tinta común: necesita altas temperaturas para adherirse a la superficie y formar letras, imágenes o gráficos.
Hay una impresora de inyección de tinta sin calor que busca reducir esto. El equipo elimina la etapa de fusión del tóner y aplica tinta líquida directamente sobre el papel, con menor consumo eléctrico y menos piezas de recambio.

articles.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Attackers are exploiting a zero-day SQL injection flaw in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, the company said in an advisory on October 22.
The flaw lets anyone who can log in to the orchestrator, even with a read-only customer account, gain operator privileges, the top level of control over it.
For on-premises orchestrators, the fix is in VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12, while Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators have already been patched.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-114625 and rated 9.9 on the CVSS scale. Orchestrators running the releases that fixed the VCO flaws exploited in July and September are still affected, because those releases are older than the new fixes.
Arista bought the VeloCloud SD-WAN product line from Broadcom, announcing the deal in July 2025. The products were earlier known as VMware SD-WAN by VeloCloud.
To exploit the flaw, an attacker needs network access to the orchestrator's web interface and a valid login. The minimum role is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in role for customer users. VCO is exposed by default, and no VCO setting prevents the exposure.
In VCO, operators create the customer and partner accounts, and each partner can manage a group of customers. The flaw allows an attacker to act as a local superuser, a role with full access. It may also allow an attacker to affect the VCO host itself and expose, modify, or disrupt the orchestrator and the data it manages.

articles.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
articles.summary:
AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22.
The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one. The risk was limited to agents who automatically signed payments and whose apps set no limits.
The missing limit is one of 25 flaws V12 found in the x402 code, and one of three it rated critical and described in detail. The x402 Foundation, which maintains the SDKs, had already fixed all three critical flaws in the August 18 releases.
One of the other two let a facilitator, the service that checks x402 payments, accept a Solana transaction that moved no tokens as a valid payment. Among the x402 SDKs, only the TypeScript one had this flaw. The other let a malicious server get an agent to sign a login message for a different website.
V12 found the flaws by reviewing the code and running local tests. Neither V12 nor the x402 Foundation has publicly reported any attacks using them.
The foundation has published no security advisory for the three flaws, and its changelogs list the fixes without calling them security fixes. As of October 23, npm audit returned no advisories for the last TypeScript releases before the fixes, and PyPI listed no vulnerabilities for the last Python release before them, The Hacker News found. Leur victime continue d’utiliser WhatsApp sans rien remarquer, car les pirates ne volent aucun mot de passe et écrivent en son nom à ses proches dans son dos.

articles.title: Fin du permis de conduire rose : voici quand il va disparaître en Europe
articles.summary:
Fin du permis de conduire rose : voici quand il va disparaître en Europe
Le compte à rebours est définitivement lancé pour le célèbre permis de conduire cartonné. D'ici quelques années, le traditionnel document rose trois volets devra obligatoirement céder sa place au format carte bancaire, beaucoup plus sécurisé. Si cette transition technologique semble encore lointaine, mieux vaut s'y préparer dès maintenant pour éviter le piège de l'amende et la saturation administrative qui s'annoncent.
Il accompagne la vie de millions d'automobilistes depuis des décennies, mais son temps est désormais compté. Le mythique permis de conduire en papier rose s'apprête à tirer sa révérence. Si ce document historique reste juridiquement valable jusqu’au 19 janvier 2033, il est devenu une véritable anomalie à l'ère du numérique et des contrôles automatisés. Moins sécurisé, très fragile et impossible à scanner rapidement par les forces de l'ordre, ce support à l'ancienne s'efface progressivement pour laisser place aux nouveaux standards européens, forçant les conducteurs à entamer une bascule obligatoire.
Pourquoi le format "carte bancaire" devient obligatoire pour tous les conducteurs
Le choix de 2033 est le résultat de la directive européenne 2006/126/CE qui impose l'harmonisation des titres de conduite au format ID-1 conforme à la norme ISO 7810. Ce format, identique à celui d'une carte bancaire, utilise le polycarbonate pour sa durabilité et ajoute une zone de lecture automatique (MRZ).

articles.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
articles.summary:
Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated.
Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw and released fixes on October 21, and applications that decode untrusted Brotli data should update.
Imperva's test did not succeed on every attempt, and code execution took several tries in its Linux arm64 setup. The result covers that one build and application setup, with other architectures and the 22.x and 26.x lines not tested. On the fixed release, 24.22.1, the same data was rejected, and no code ran.
The demonstration goes beyond the first public proof of concept, which achieved code execution only on a deliberately weakened test build. On a standard build, that proof of concept's author reported a crash and a limited read of process memory, not code execution, and said a working attack on a normal build was not achieved.
No exploitation of the flaw in the wild has been reported as of October 22.
Which Applications Are Affected
The flaw is in the Brotli decoder that Node.js bundles, so it affects applications on the 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines, not only the one build Imperva tested. A service reaches that decoder from either side of an HTTP exchange: when it reads a Brotli-compressed res…

articles.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
articles.summary:
Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.
The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.
Ghostscript can read a name chosen by an attacker as instructions rather than as a file, and point it to a second file that carries commands to run. Pillow's maintainers fixed it in version 13.0.0, released on October 16.
Pillow turns up almost everywhere Python handles images: web upload forms, avatar and thumbnail tools, document and PDF pipelines, and most machine-learning projects pull it in. OX Security, the firm whose report drew attention to the flaws, estimates the library is downloaded about 436 million times a month.
Version 13.0.0 is a large security release, with fixes across four severity levels, from low to critical, two of which are rated critical by the maintainers. None of the flaws is known to be under attack.
The weakness is the filename, not the picture. "The flaw is triggered by the filename, not by anything in the PostScript document," the advisory says, meaning a harmless EPS file can still cause damage when an attacker sets its name. That makes upload endpoints that keep or build a stored file's name from user input the realistic target.

articles.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Used New Mesh Network Backdoor in Destructive Ukraine Attack
articles.summary:
The Russian state-sponsored hacking group Sandworm teamed up with another threat actor to carry out a destructive wiping attack targeting a Ukrainian logistics company last year.
According to ESET, the attack involved UAC-0099 (aka Earth Sirrush) obtaining initial access to the target on July 16, 2025, via a spear-phishing email bearing a malware-laced attachment that led to the deployment of the MATCHWOK backdoor through a downloader called MATCHBOIL.
The activity ultimately culminated with the threat actor handing off access to Sandworm, which then conducted a data-wiping attack on September 17, 2025, more than two months after it obtained a foothold.
What makes the attack stand out is UAC-0099's use of a previously undocumented backdoor called MythicRatatoskr that communicates with a command-and-control (C2) server hosted inside the Yggdrasil mesh network. The backdoor was deployed a day after MATCHWOK was executed.
There are indications that development on the backdoor started sometime between December 2024 and February 2025. Its functionality is fairly straightforward in that it sends victim metadata to the C2 server, poll for new commands, transmit command output, take screenshots, and upload/download files.
It can also alter the current working directory, enumerate directory contents, change the C2 server URL, execute a shell command via "cmd.exe," and spawn a reverse SOCKS5 proxy. In addition, some artifacts include a 10-minute startup delay in a likely effort to avoi…

Xbox Misses Microsoft's Executive Pay Target for the Fifth Time in Six Years
Microsoft's Xbox division has missed a performance goal tied to executive pay for the fifth time in six years. articles.title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Risk Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
articles.summary:
PHP has warned of another way an attacker could run code on a web server, two days after it shipped emergency fixes for the critical PHP2Shell flaws.
The new issue, assigned CVE-2026-115560, affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk.
The project is not issuing an emergency fix for it. Instead, it recommends turning off a feature called session upload progress until a fix is available in the next routine release.
The warning came in a short informational advisory published on October 23. It follows the October 21 emergency release that fixed two critical PHP2Shell flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which let an attacker without an account run code on a server. Those were patched in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The new issue is separate and is not fixed by those releases.
Only a narrow setup is at risk. PHP says the problem can occur when a web application does all of the following: sets the session.serialize_handler option to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration, then changes that option to php while running by calling ini_set(), and makes that change before it calls session_start().
Session upload progress must also still be turned on. An application that never changes the serialize handler while running can leave the feature on and is not exposed through this path. PHP says this setup is unlikely in practice.

articles.title: Ruby Fixes Three Regex Engine Bugs Responsible for Four Critical GitLab RCE Flaws
articles.summary:
Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to fix three bugs in Onigmo, the regular expression engine built into the language. The bugs lie behind four critical security flaws that GitLab patched over the past month.
GitLab found that a specially crafted pattern could corrupt memory while Ruby compiles it, potentially leading to code execution on its own servers.
Ruby says any application that builds a regular expression from text an attacker controls is affected, not just GitLab.
Which Applications Are Affected
In its advisory, Ruby said an application is affected only if it compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls. That happens when a program passes such a string to Regexp.new, Regexp.union or Regexp.compile, or places it inside a pattern through interpolation, as in /#{input}/.
Applications that only use regular expressions written by their own developers are not affected.
Ruby fixed the bugs in 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13. The 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 releases are the first in their series to carry any of the three fixes.
An earlier release from the same week, 4.0.8, does not include the fix for one of the flaws, CVE-2026-110264, so 4.0 users should install 4.0.9.
Ruby 3.2 and earlier will not get a fix. Ruby 3.2 reached end of life on April 1, 2026, and 3.2.11 was its final release. Ruby recommends moving to 3.4 or 4.0.
If you cannot upgrade yet, the advisory says to stop compiling regular expressions from untrusted input.

OptiScaler is a community-driven project that seeks to bring the benefits of upscaling and frame-generation across brands of GPUs, so gamers don't miss out on playability if the game doesn't feature the upscaler/frame-gen tech provided by their GPU vendor. The community successfully modded AMD FSR 4.1.2 to work on Intel Arc GPUs, leveraging the Intel XMX cores (Xe Math Extensions). Current implementations of FSR on Arc relies on a fallback DP4a path that offers significantly lower performance benefit.
DarkerThanLpDark on Reddit put FSR 4.1.2 Lite on Arc B580 to the test in "Clair Obscur: Expedition 33," comparing its performance with the game's native XeSS implementation, and FSR's standard DP4a implementation on Arc GPUs. The updater belongs to Time4Popcorn, an abandoned copy of Popcorn Time, a free app that streamed pirated films and TV over BitTorrent.
Popcorn Time was popular about a decade ago, and the original shut down in 2014, but several copies kept running under the same name. A separate, legal project that took the Popcorn Time name in early 2025 is unrelated to it.
Eye Security, which monitors client networks for threats, found the updater during a routine threat hunt: a program called Updater.exe on one client's laptop kept trying to reach a web address that was no longer registered.
The firm registered the address itself to see what would connect, and about 50 requests a second poured in. It later laid out the operation, which it named Operation IXIM, in a write-up and a talk at Hack.lu on October 22.
Over six months, those requests carried more than 3.8 million different hardware IDs. The IDs proved an unreliable way to count machines, because some Windows PCs shared one and some Macs changed theirs, so Eye revised its estimate to 2.5 to 3 million Windows computers and 250,000 to 350,000 Macs.

articles.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Behind Node.js RCE Also Affects Bun, Python and Other Widely Used Software
articles.summary:
A memory-corruption flaw in Google's Brotli decoder sits in many programs that unpack Brotli-compressed data, among them Bun, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages, and Envoy proxies set up to decompress Brotli.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, the flaw allows crafted compressed data to overwrite past the end of a buffer and corrupt a program's memory, potentially causing a crash, a memory leak, or the execution of attacker-controlled code.
Imperva researchers have shown that code can run on one unpatched Node.js build. The same has not been demonstrated on the other software, and no real-world attacks have been reported.
The flaw was first disclosed on October 21, when Node.js and Google shipped fixes, and more have followed product by product since. Because the bug is in Google's decoder and each program ships its own copy of it, every one has to update that copy on its own.
Brotli is a compression format from Google, used across the web to shrink pages and other traffic. The bug is in the C code that unpacks a Brotli stream, so it travels into anything that reuses that code, from language runtimes to proxies to Python packages.

articles.title: Starlink fonctionne à nouveau correctement en Ukraine
articles.summary:
Le polémique Starlink en Ukraine s'achève. Le service offert par la société d'Elon Musk fonctionne de nouveau correctement dans ce pays.
C'est une polémique qui a duré presque une dizaine de jours. Le 14 octobre, on apprenait que les terminaux Starlink allant à plus de 160 kilomètres par heure avaient été bridés. Depuis, Elon Musk a expliqué que ça n'était pas de sa faute, pointant indirectement du doigt Donald Trump, qui a lui aussi nié toute responsabilité. Un problème qui avait duré, de manière irrégulière, jusqu'à aujourd'hui.
Starlink offre à nouveau des vitesses allant au-delà des 400 km/h en Ukraine
Les problèmes sont finis du côté de la connexion Starlink en Ukraine (pour le moment tout du moins). En effet, ce n'est plus seulement une annonce - plus ou moins douteuse - émanant des États-Unis, mais un constat fait directement du côté de Kiev.
« Les systèmes de surveillance du ministère de la Défense indiquent un retour à la vitesse normale pour Starlink/Starshield. Nous enregistrons une vitesse supérieure à 400 km/h. La connexion est stable » a ainsi assuré le ministre de la Défense ukrainnienne, Ievheniy Khmara, à des journalistes, selon Reuters.
Les responsabilités restent très floues
Le ministre est resté par contre - de manière compréhensible - évasif sur la vitesse maximale que peuvent atteindre les terminaux Starlink tout en fonctionnant normalement. Il a simplement indiqué que « les systèmes de surveillance avaient précédemment signalé des perturbations du servi…

articles.title: Une IA d’Anthropic cache un message dans les étoiles et c'est... celle d’OpenAI qui le déchiffre
articles.summary:
Au-dessus du lac de montagne dessiné par Claude Fable 5.1, chaque étoile est une lettre, lue d’après sa hauteur dans le ciel. Personne n’avait indiqué au modèle d’Anthropic comment cacher sa phrase, et GPT-6 Astra, chez OpenAI, a pu déchiffrer 44 des 50 images à message caché produites par Fable.
Bryan Chan et trois autres chercheurs du programme SASH ont confié cinquante courtes phrases à Claude Fable 5.1, dans quinze langues. Le modèle devait les dissimuler dans une image d'apparence ordinaire, sans écrire le secret nulle part. Une seconde session de Fable recevait ensuite une simple capture de l'image, sans son code source, et devait dire si l'image contenait un message, puis le restituer. Les équipes de sécurité ont tout intérêt à connaître ces procédés, car des agents d'OpenAI ont glissé des données dans des images lors du piratage de Hugging Face, cet été.
Des lettres rangées par hauteur, que GPT-6 Astra lit mieux que Fable
Fable a choisi la hauteur dans 33 images sur 50. Le modèle a aligné des immeubles ou des étoiles, et plus un objet était haut, plus sa lettre arrivait loin dans l'alphabet. Fable a dessiné une ville de nuit dans 23 images, où chaque immeuble donne une lettre et chaque groupe d'immeubles un mot, tandis que la lune et le décor sont de simples ornements. Quand l'alphabet latin ne suffisait plus, le modèle a complété le décor. articles.title: iPhone Duo : Safari rencontre des problèmes d’affichage, Apple cherche une solution
articles.summary:
Sur l’écran extérieur de l’iPhone Duo, une colonne de commandes dans Safari grignote la place réservée aux pages web. La marque à la pomme reconnaît le défaut et dit chercher comment y remédier.
À 2 339 euros minimum, l’iPhone Duo n’échappe pas à la critique, notamment sur un point précis : la navigation dans Safari sur son écran externe de 5,4 pouces. Dans un billet de blog WebKit consacré à Safari 27.1, Jen Simmons admet que les sites ne peuvent pas, pour l’instant, occuper toute la surface disponible. Apple n’avance aucune date, mais demande aux développeurs de lui soumettre leurs idées.
Safari laisse une partie de l’écran inutilisée sur l’iPhone Duo
Sur l’écran externe de 5,4 pouces, les commandes de Safari occupent une bande sur le côté droit. Les sites web ne peuvent pas s’étendre derrière ces éléments et leur zone d’affichage s’en trouve, par conséquent, réduite. Apple a choisi cette disposition pour préserver de la place en hauteur, mais elle limite la largeur disponible pour consulter les pages.
L’équipe WebKit a reconnu cette contrainte dans une publication consacrée à Safari 27.1. Jen Simmons, qui travaille sur le navigateur, explique qu’Apple souhaite donner aux développeurs davantage de possibilités pour exploiter cette surface. Un site pourrait notamment étendre l’arrière-plan de son en-tête sur toute la largeur de l’écran, y compris derrière les commandes.
Apple cherche une solution qui ne masque pas le contenu des sites
